items.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "echo ---i3c_cpu1---; ls /sys/bus/i3c 2>&1; sudo i3cdetect -l 2>&1; ls /sys/bus/i3c/devices 2>&1; dmesg | grep -iE 'i3c.*(cpu[1]|i3c[0-9])' | tail -20; dmesg | grep -iE 'i3c|i2c' | tail -10"
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL kernel/sysfs I3C presence + dmesg i3c/i2c lines so the user confirms the CPU1 I3C controller/bus is enumerated per spec; actual I3C target probe may need vendor i3c tooling.
items.risk: RISK: I3C probing needs vendor tooling that may not be installed; agent reports sysfs/dmesg enumeration and leaves the deep I3C probe to the operator if tooling is absent.

items.ai_commands: -- Link flap: repeat link up/down 5x per port via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for i in $(seq 1 5); do ip link set ${IFACE:?operator must set the target NIC interface name} down; sleep 1; ip link set ${IFACE:?operator must set the target NIC interface name} up; sleep 2; ip link show ${IFACE:?operator must set the target NIC interface name}; done 2>&1" then check the interface + BMC network recovered.
items.ai_logs_output: return the 5x link flap loop output (link state per iteration) + final `ip link show` + BMC ping check so the user confirms the NIC and BMC network survived.
items.risk: RISK: link flapping drops networking on that port 5x; use a non-management test port to avoid losing the SSH session.

items.ai_commands: -- Resolution change up - 1920x1200x16bit: change the Mini-DP video resolution/color depth up to 1920x1200@16bit in the OS display settings. 【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check TPM 2.0 Presence and Status on Linux
Here are the steps to verify if your system has TPM 2.0 and to check its status:

# Install necessary tools
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install tpm2-tools

# Check if TPM is detected
tpm2_getcap -c properties-fixed

# Check the TPM version
tpm2_getcap -c properties-variable | grep TPM_PT_REVISION

2. Interact with the TPM 2.0 Chip
Use tpm2-tools to interact with the TPM:

# Read PCR values
tpm2_pcrread

# Take ownership of TPM (if not already taken)
tpm2_takeownership -o ownerpass -e endorsepass -l lockpass

# More TPM interactions (e.g., generating keys)
tpm2_createprimary -C o -g sha256 -G rsa -c primary.ctx
tpm2_create -C primary.ctx -G rsa -u key.pub -r key.priv
tpm2_load -C primary.ctx -u key.pub -r key.priv -c key.ctx

3. Prepare for BitLocker Integration
Since BitLocker is a Windows feature, you'll need a Windows environment to test full BitLocker functionality. However, you can prepare your system and understand how to use TPM 2.0 on Windows through Linux:

Dual Boot: Install Windows on a secondary partition or use a virtual machine (e.g., VirtualBox, VMWare) with TPM passthrough enabled.
BitLocker Setup on Windows:
Enable TPM in BIOS: Ensure the TPM 2.0 module is enabled in your BIOS/UEFI settings.
Check TPM on Windows: Boot into Windows and use tpm.msc to verify TPM status.
BitLocker: Use the manage-bde command or BitLocker GUI to enable BitLocker encryption.
4. Testing BitLocker
Once BitLocker is enabled, you can ensure that it is utilizing TPM 2.0 by checking the BitLocker status and ensuring that the TPM is used for key protection.

# Check BitLocker status (in Windows Command Prompt)
manage-bde -status

# To enable BitLocker (in Windows with TPM)
manage-bde -on C: -tpmandpin -pin <your_pin>

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enable BitLocker Without TPM
First, you need to configure your Windows policy to allow BitLocker without a TPM.

Using Group Policy Editor
Open the Group Policy Editor:

Press Win + R, type gpedit.msc, and press Enter.
Navigate to the BitLocker Policy:

Go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > BitLocker Drive Encryption > Operating System Drives.
Configure Policy:

Find the policy Require additional authentication at startup and double-click to edit it.
Enable the policy.
Ensure the option Allow BitLocker without a compatible TPM (requires a password or a startup key on a USB flash drive) is checked.
Click Apply and OK.
2. Enable BitLocker on a Drive
Once the policy is set, you can proceed to enable BitLocker.

Using BitLocker GUI
Open File Explorer:

Right-click on the drive you want to encrypt (e.g., C: drive).
Select Turn on BitLocker.
Choose Authentication Method:

Select Enter a password or Insert a USB flash drive.
Follow the prompts to set a password or use a USB flash drive.
Save Recovery Key:

Save the recovery key to a file, print it, or store it somewhere safe.
Encrypt the Drive:

Choose the type of encryption (New or Compatible mode).
Start the encryption process.
Using Command Line
You can also use the manage-bde command-line tool to enable BitLocker.

Open Command Prompt as Administrator:

Press Win + X, then select Command Prompt (Admin) or Windows PowerShell (Admin).
Enable BitLocker with a Password:

manage-bde -on C: -password
Follow Prompts:

Enter and confirm the password when prompted.
Save Recovery Key:

manage-bde -protectors -add C: -rp
3. Check BitLocker Status
To verify that BitLocker is enabled and working without a TPM, check the status.

GUI Method
Open BitLocker Drive Encryption:
Go to Control Panel > System and Security > BitLocker Drive Encryption.
Ensure that the drive is listed as BitLocker On.
Command Line Method
Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
Check Status:
manage-bde -status C:
This command will show the status of BitLocker on the specified drive, including the encryption method and the protectors used.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Attempt to apply a corrupt update image for the BIOS active/recovery region.
2. Update Corrupt capsule image

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: 1. AST1060 should reject the update
items.ai_packages_needed: a deliberately corrupt / older BIOS image (user-provided) + curl + BMC creds
items.ai_commands: -- Reject BIOS Update with Corruptu pdate Image: attempt to update the BIOS with a corrupt update image / an older (downgrade) image and confirm the BMC rejects it (ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" mc info 2>&1 unchanged, update task returns an error). State-changing attempt that must be rejected.
items.ai_logs_output: return the UpdateService POST error + the pre/post BIOS version (unchanged) so the user confirms the bad/downgrade image was rejected without changing firmware.
items.risk: RISK: using a corrupt/older image is safe only because it must be rejected; never flash a working newer image in this test.

[global]
bs=512

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    IOmeter is a storage stress tool. For this test, it is used to test the PCIe and nvme communication busses.

1. Configure each drive as its own volume.
2. Boot to OS
3. Install IOmeter software.
4. Bring all HDD/SSD/NVME drives online and format
5. Run IOmeter.
6. Select the system in the “Topology” box to the left.
7. Under the “Disk Targets” Tab,
a. Select all volumes in the “Targets” box.
b. Set “# of Outstanding I/Os” to 16.
8. Under the “Access Specifications” Tab
a. Select “Default” in the box to the right, and click “Add”
9. Under the “Results Display” Tab
a. In the “Results Since” box click “Start of Test” to monitor the test progress
10. Click the Green Flag to begin the tests
11. IOmeter writes a test file to each volume if it is not already present. For larger storage footprints,
this can take several hours to complete. While IOmeter is doing this, it will display “Preparing
Drives” in an info bar.
12. After this, it will display bar graphs depicting the current results
13. The test should run for a minimum of 48 hours with no reported errors.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Pass: Test should run with no reported errors, system hangs, or reboots
items.ai_commands: -- IOmeter benchmark is a GUI-driven tool typically run interactively; needs IOmeter installed + a workload config. Agent can launch the configured IOmeter worker headless if a scriptable config is provided.
items.ai_logs_output: return the IOmeter result CSV/log so user diffs against expected performance. Long sustained run - confirm approval.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To validate HDD hot adding function that if a drive was not present in a slot during boot, a drive can be recognized well and handle correctly.

Windows:
1. Boot into Windows OS without HDD/SSD drive installed in a slot. 
2. Plug in HDD/SSD drive into slot for 4 seconds,
3. Check disk manager whether can show installed HDD/SSD drive information.
4. Have IO stress for NVMe drive 5 minutes.

items.ai_commands: -- Driver Installation: install the MLNX-OFED driver. Agent mounts the MLNX ISO and runs mlnxofedinstall sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mkdir -p /tmp/mst 2>&1; mount MLNX_Packages/MLNX_OFED_LINUX-5.8-1.1.2.1-ubuntu22.04-x86_64.iso /tmp/mst 2>&1; cd /tmp/mst && yes | ./mlnxofedinstall --force 2>&1 | tail -n 20 2>&1"; requires the MLNX-ISO on the host and a reboot afterwards.

items.items: AC Power Cycle (via PDU) ( with revise MAC address)
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Before run AC cycle,  revise BMC and others eth MAC address
1. Eth MAC command:
ifconfig <device port> down
ifconfig <device port>  hw ether XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
ifconfig <device port>  up

2. BMC MAC command:
ipmitool raw 0x30 0x40 0x0
ipmitool lan set 0x01 macaddr XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
ex.
ipmitool lan set 0x01 macaddr 70:e2:84:3a:65:10

AC:
check all of devices in each cycle time.
1. Set node power policy for "Always-On".
2. SUT records the information of "lspci -vv" when booting into OS.
3. After lspci information recorded, shutdown SUT.
4. Turn off chassis AC power via Cyber Switch.
5. Wait for 30 seconds and AC on.
6. Wait for the time that SUT should boot into OS for recording lspci information and shutdown (For example, 600 seconds).
7. Repeat step 2 to step 6 long term.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. SUT should not hang during AC cycle.
2. Information of "lspci", "lsblk", "nvme" commands should not have any change during AC cycle.
3. SUT should be workable after AC cycle stress.
4. BMC FRU and SDR information for each cycle should be correct.
items.ai_commands: -- AC Power Cycle (via PDU) ( with revise MAC address): AC power cycling (via PDU/Cyber Switch) + recording lspci/lsblk/nvme across cycles requires physical PDU control; agent can automate the per-cycle data capture sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci -vv 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cycle_lspci.txt; lsblk 2>&1; nvme list 2>&1" but the actual AC cut/restore is operator (via the switched PDU).
items.ai_logs_output: return the per-cycle lspci/lsblk/nvme capture so the user diffs that device information is unchanged across AC cycles; AC on/off is operator via the PDU.
items.risk: RISK: AC power cycling will interrupt the host and possibly the BMC; run only on a dedicated SUT via a controllable PDU, operator initiates the cut.

items.items: Upgrade and downgrade via broadcom tools in Linux OS
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Put fw tool in Linux OS
$unzip g4Xdiagnostics_linux.zip
2. Check PCIe Switch Firmware file into the same folder. (Please check the veriosn should be the latest one.)
Miramar_PCIe_SW1_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw Miramar_PCIe_SW2_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
Miramar_PCIe_SW3_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
Miramar_PCIe_SW4_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
3. There are four PCIe Switches (PEX89144) in the system, please list and check PCIe Switches as below command.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 --list
It should show eight PEX89144 devices as below picture.
The devices 1 and 2 belong to PCIe Switch 1 (SW1).
The devices 3 and 4 belong to PCIe Switch 2 (SW2).
The devices 5 and 6 belong to PCIe Switch 3 (SW3).
The devices 7 and 8 belong to PCIe Switch 4 (SW4).
4. Updated PCIe SW1-4 firmware image.
Before updating, you may need to check current PCIe SW1 firmware version as below command.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 1 show
Updating the required firmware to SW1 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 1 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW1_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW2 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 3 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW2_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW3 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 5 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW3_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW4 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 7 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW4_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
5. Restart the system to make the fresh image active.
# reboot
6. The PCIe Switch 1-4 (SW1-4) firmware version should be updated as expected.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i [1,3,5,7] show

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.procedure:

    【During Test】
    1. Boot into setup menu and configure the BMC IP to DHCP option. Then save and exit.
2. Boot into BIOS setup menu again for checking the IP address.
3. Login to BMC web UI with the DHCP IP
4. Boot into setup menu and configure a BMC static IP. Then save and exit.
5. Boot into BIOS setup menu again for checking the IP address.
6. Login to BMC web UI with the static IP

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.

items.criteria:
1. BMC should get a DHCP IP and could be pinged and log into BMC web UI successfully
2. BMC should be set to static IP and could be pinged and log into BMC web UI successfully
items.ai_commands: -- BMC network configuration→Lan channel Configuration Address: read the BMC LAN channel configuration (address source, IP, MAC) ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP|MAC|Subnet|Source".
items.ai_logs_output: return the LAN channel print (address source/IP/netmask/MAC) so the user confirms the BIOS-listed BMC network config matches ipmitool.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Log in to BIOS when no password setting
2. Set an Administrator password (Within the defined range)
3. Save change and reset
4. Log in to BIOS with wrong password (3 times)
5. Log in to BIOS with correct Administrator password
6. Clear Administrator password (Set new password without enter any word)
7. Save change and reset
8. Log in to BIOS again without password

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. System should boot into BIOS when no password setting
2. Password should be set within the deined range with supported characters
3. System should not be able to enter BIOS with wrong password
4. System should boot into BIOS with correct password
5. Password should be clear successfully
items.ai_commands: -- Administrator Password: setting/verifying the BIOS Administrator Password is a BIOS-Security-page UI action (set a password, reboot, verify prompt); requires a person at the BIOS console and risks locking the platform if lost.
items.ai_logs_output: operator sets the admin password and confirms the BIOS prompts on next entry; agent cannot drive the BIOS UI.
items.risk: RISK: a lost admin password can lock BIOS access; human-only with the credentials recorded.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Secure Boot feature is Active if Secure Boot is Enabled, Platform Key (PK) is enrolled and the System is in User mode. The mode change requires platform reset [Enable/Disable]
1. In CSM configuration, set all item to UEFI and disable CSM.
2. Enable secure boot with build-in factory key loaded.
3. Install OS via any media.
4. Disable secure boot(unsigned OS) with below command:\
     "sudo update-secureboot-policy" \
     Follow insctrction to disable secure boot.
5. Reboot system, press any key when you see the MOK management
6. Select Change Secure Boot state,than enter passowrd you set in step4 as request.
7. Boot should fail with unsigned OS.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. System could boot to BIOS after setting
2. System able to boot with signed OS when secure boot is enable.
3. System cannot be boot with unsigned OS when secure boot is enable.
items.ai_commands: -- Secure Boot: verify the Secure Boot state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mokutil --sb-state 2>&1; dmesg | grep -iE 'Secure boot|secureboot' | head -n 10 2>&1"; enabling/disabling Secure Boot itself is a BIOS-Security-page UI change (human step), the OS state read is automated.
items.ai_logs_output: return `mokutil --sb-state` + the firmware/OS secure-boot dmesg so the user confirms the Secure Boot state per the BIOS Security page.

# Check NUMA node configuration after operator sets BIOS NPS (NPS1/2/4)

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enable WOL function in OS
2. Enable WOL function in BIOS setup menu (and in NIC card option ROM if necessary)
3. Set SUT power state to S5 in BIOS setup menu
4. Save change and reset into OS
5. Shutdown the SUT (graceful shutdown)
6. Send an magic packet to SUT from a client
    Linux client: ether-wake -i ethX <MAC address>
    Windows client: Download the command line tool from "https://www.depicus.com/wake-on-lan/wake-on-lan-cmd" and follow the instruction in the web page to execute it.
7. Shutdown the SUT (graceful shutdown) and unplug AC power
8. Wait 10 seconds and plug AC power back
9. Send an magic packet to SUT from a client
10. Repeat step 5 to step 9 for WOL disable

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. WOL function should be Enabled successfully
2. Magic packet should be sent without any error
3. System should be woken successfully
4. WOL function should be Disabled successfully
5. Magic packet should be sent without any error when WOL disable
6. System should NOT be woken when WOL disable
7. BMC IP should be alive without lose
items.ai_commands: -- WOL function test: WOL function test. Agent (as the wake client from the peer host) sends the magic packet sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo ethtool $DUT_NIC 2>&1; echo 'client sends magic packet'; ether-wake -i $DUT_NIC $DUT_MAC 2>&1"; the SUT must be in S5 (graceful shutdown), which needs an operator to set S5/WOL in the OS+BIOS and to unplug/re-plug AC for the disable case.
items.ai_logs_output: return the ether-wake magic-packet send result + the ping/WOL wake status so the user confirms the system wakes when WOL is enabled and does not when disabled; operator handles the S5/AC steps.

items.items: Upgrade and Downgrade BMC firmware by Redfish when system is booted
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade BMC firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory
items.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + BMC image (user provides)
items.ai_commands: -- BMC downgrade via Redfish (system is booted): the agent needs the exact user-provided BMC image first the SUT must be booted first and the host OS running for the flash, then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active after BMC reset only one time. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
items.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the BMC version changed, only one BMC reset happened, and the SUT still boots/passes self-checks.
items.risk: RISK: BMC firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.  Flash BMC Firmware :
        Follow the standard procedure to perform the first BMC firmware flash.
        Ensure you follow the official firmware update guidelines during this process.

    2.  Second BMC Firmware Update :
        Begin the second BMC firmware update.
        At some point during the update process,  AC power to the server to simulate an unexpected power interruption.

    3. Expected Outcome:
        After the server is powered off, reconnect the AC power.
        The system should automatically detect the simulated BMC firmware crash and initiate recovery.

    【After Test】

    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. The BMC firmware should automatically revert to the previous stable version, which was the state after the initial BMC firmware flash.
2. The server should boot normally, and the BMC firmware should return to normal operation.
items.ai_packages_needed: BMC firmware images + human AC power control + BMC recovery procedure
items.ai_commands: -- Crash BMC and recovery: crash-and-recover the BMC by cutting AC power mid-firmware-update to simulate a crash, then verifying the BMC auto-reverts to the previous stable firmware. Requires a person to physically cut/restore AC power and an operator to drive the two BMC firmware flashes; the agent cannot simulate the power interruption nor boot the BMC flash recovery console.
items.ai_logs_output: operator performs the two firmware flashes with the intentional AC cut at the second update, re-applies AC and records the revert to the previous firmware + normal BMC boot; agent cannot produce this evidence.
items.risk: RISK: crashing the BMC mid-flash and AC-cycling is physically destructive to the BMC firmware state; human-only, perform carefully on a test unit.

    NOTE:"Multiple Mount" means that you can use multiple different mount methods (such as HTTP, HTTPS, NFS, CIFS) to mount different image files at the same time. This allows you to use multiple different images on the same server for different operations, such as installing different operating systems or software.

1. Make sure you have multiple image files available and know the location or URL for each image file.
2. Connect to the target server's BMC using SSH or otherwise.
3. After logging in to BMC, enter the OpenBMC console.
4. Image mount using OpenBMC's Web GUI. From the remote console interface, select Media -> Activate, then select Media -> Mount virtual media.
5. For each image file, perform the following steps in order:
    In the "Mount Media File from Network" option, enter the URL or path to the image file.

    From the "Local Media Mounted" section, select the format of the image, then click "Browse" to find the image file, click "Open", and then click "Mount".
6. Once complete, you can perform operations on the mounted ISO, such as installing an operating system.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.ai_packages_needed: net-snmp + a 2nd host; BMC SNMP agent configured by operator
items.ai_commands: -- SNMP Trap verifies the BMC SNMP agent/trap functionality; it needs a management/trap-receiver host and enabling/configuring SNMP on the BMC Web UI (community/v3 + trap destination). Agent can from the trap receiver run `snmpget -v2c -c ${SNMP_COMMUNITY:?operator must set SNMP community (v2c) or v3 creds} "$BMC_IP" system.sysDescr.0 2>&1` to sanity-check the agent after it is configured by the operator.
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL snmpget/walk output confirming the BMC SNMP agent responds for the SNMP Trap mode; the trap destination/receiver setup + Web UI enable is the operator part.
items.risk: RISK: enabling SNMP + pointing traps is a config change on the BMC; needs a 2nd host as trap receiver and read-only community.

Use NetSNMP to check.

items.ai_packages_needed: snmpwalk (net-snmp), BMC SNMP agent must be enabled + community configured
items.ai_commands: -- SNMP "monitor_systemHealth" monitoring reads specific BMC MIB data via the SNMP agent; from a 2nd management host run `snmpwalk -v2c -c ${SNMP_COMMUNITY:?operator must set SNMP community (v2c) or v3 creds} "$BMC_IP" .1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3.2.1.2 | grep -i health (or walk the vendor MIB subtree once the SNMP community/v3 creds + MIB are configured). Enable + point SNMP agent first.
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL snmpwalk output for the system health OID subtree so the user confirms the monitor_systemHealth SNMP data is correct.
items.risk: RISK: SNMP queries need a management host + enabled/configured SNMP agent on the BMC (community/v3 + firewall); enabling SNMP is a config change, and some BMC SNMP sets expose credentials - use read-only community.

    【During Test】
    1. Login to OpenBMC Web GUI: Open a browser and enter the IP address or hostname of the target OpenBMC server to access the Web GUI. Sign in with your login credentials.
2. Find User Management Options: Once logged in, look for options related to user management. This may be found in the User Accounts, Permissions, Authentication, etc. sections.
3. Set up users: In the user management area, you can create, edit or manage user accounts. Make sure that the user account you set has appropriate permissions for subsequent setting operations.

4. Look for Zeroconf or Network settings: In OpenBMC's Web GUI, look for options related to Zeroconf or Network settings. This may be found in sections such as network settings, connectivity, or system settings.

5. Enable Zeroconf or mDNS: In Zeroconf or Network Settings, look for an option to enable Zeroconf or mDNS. This may have a switch or option that lets you enable Zeroconf or mDNS functionality.

6.Save Settings: After making a setting change, make sure to save the settings.

7. Restart service or system (if required): In some cases, configuration changes may require restarting network services or the OpenBMC system to apply the changes. Please refer to the relevant documentation to determine if this is required.

8 .Test Zeroconf: When you're done with the setup, other Zeroconf-capable devices should be able to discover your OpenBMC server on the same LAN.

    【After Test】

    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.items: Set LAN source in DHCP via BMC
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set LAN source by:
    - IPMI command - Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> ipsrc dhcp.
    - Web UI - Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Configuration" -> Click "Network" -> Check "Use DHCP".
2. Send command: ipmitool lan print to check LAN information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: BMC LAN should get an IP address from DHCP server.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 ipsrc dhcp 2>&1; echo ---lan-print---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address Source|MAC Address|IP Address" ; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -i firmware
items.ai_logs_output: set ch1 LAN source to DHCP then return the FULL `ipmitool lan print` output (IP Address Source, MAC, IP) plus a `mc info` firmware line, so the user confirms the BMC pulled an IP from the DHCP server.
items.risk: RISK: write to BMC network config (ipsrc dhcp) can drop/re-address the active BMC connection on the managed channel; use a non-management channel and confirm connectivity after.

items.items: Set LAN source in static via BMC
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set LAN source by:
    - IPMI command - Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> ipsrc static.
    - Web UI - Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Configuration" -> Click "Network" -> Uncheck "Use DHCP".
2. Set static IP:
     - IPMI command -
          Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> ipaddr <x.x.x.x>
          Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> netmask <x.x.x.x>
          Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> defgw ipaddr <x.x.x.x>
    - Web UI -
          Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Configuration" -> Click "Network".
          Type IP address in the column of "IPv4 address".
          Type netmask in the column of "Subnet mask".
          Type default gateway IP address in the column of "Default Gateway".
3. Send command: ipmitool lan print to check LAN information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: BMC LAN should display correctly as setting.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 ipsrc static 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 ipaddr "$DUT_IP" 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 netmask 255.255.255.0 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 defgw ip 2>&1; echo ---lan-print---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address Source|IP Address|Subnet Mask|Default Gateway"
items.ai_logs_output: set ch1 LAN source to static with the target IP/netmask then return the FULL `ipmitool lan print` address lines so the user confirms the BMC shows the static IP exactly as configured.
items.risk: RISK: write to BMC network config (ipsrc static + IP) re-addresses the active BMC channel and can drop the current connection; confirm the static IP/network before applying and that it persists.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Access Redfish Endpoint:
    Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog.
2. Check Date and Service Status:
    Verify that the "DateTimeLocalOffset" and "DateTime" match the BMC web interface.
    Ensure that "ServiceEnabled" is set to true.
3. Customize BMC Event Log:
    Log in to the BMC from the web interface.
    Go to "Events" → "Event Log".
    Open "Customize Table" and make sure all columns are selected, then click "OK".
4. Generate Events:
    Ensure that the system log contains at least one info, one warning, and one error event.
5. Access Redfish Log Entries:
    Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog/Entries.
6. Compare Entries:
    Compare the entries in the "PlatformLog Entries" with the BMC web "Event Log".
    Verify that "Severity," "Source," "Message," "Created," "CommonEventID," "Serviceable," and "TotalSequenceNumber" match.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
Critical content in Redfish and the WebGUI log should match.
Log entries with different severities (OK, Warning, Critical) should be verified and matched between Redfish and the BMC web interface.
items.ai_commands: echo "=== LogServices collection (canonical: Managers/bmc) ==="; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices -H "Content-Type: application/json" | jq '.Members[]?"@odata.id"'; echo "=== sample entries per service (Journal/Dump/FaultLog known real on Wistron) ==="; for svc in Journal Dump FaultLog; do echo "### $svc"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/$svc/Entries" -H "Content-Type: application/json" | jq '.Entries?[:5] | [.[] | {Severity,Message,EntryType,Created}]'; done; echo "=== SEL/OEM count (Journal FaultLog) ==="; for svc in Journal FaultLog; do echo "### $svc"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/$svc/Entries" | jq '.Entries? // [] | [.[] | select((.EntryType // "") | test("SEL|OEM";"i"))] | length'; done
items.ai_logs_output: returns the LogServices collection + first 5 entries of each log service (Journal/Dump/FaultLog) + SEL/OEM count; user confirms remote-syslog/SEL entries present. Path per Wistron 11/12.RestAPI: /redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices{,/Journal|Dump|FaultLog,Entries}.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Access Redfish Endpoint:
        Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog.
2. Check Date and Service Status:
        Verify that the "DateTimeLocalOffset" and "DateTime" match the BMC web interface.
        Ensure that "ServiceEnabled" is set to true.
3. Customize BMC Event Log:
        Log in to the BMC from the web interface.
        Go to "Events" → "Event Log".
        Open "Customize Table" and make sure all columns are selected, then click "OK".
4. Generate Events:
        Ensure that the system log contains at least one info, one warning, and one error event.
5.  Access Redfish Log Entries:
        Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog/Entries.
6. Compare Entries:
        Compare the entries in the "PlatformLog Entries" with the BMC web "Event Log".
        Verify that "Severity," "Source," "Message," "Created," "CommonEventID," "Serviceable," and "TotalSequenceNumber" match.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
Critical content in Redfish and the WebGUI log should match.
    Log entries with different severities (OK, Warning, Critical) should be verified and matched between Redfish and the BMC web interface.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -i syslog; echo ---; bash -c 'cat /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null; grep -rhE "^\*\." /etc/rsyslog* 2>/dev/null' | grep remote; echo ---; ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "$DUT_USER@$DUT_IP" 'grep -iE "redfish|syslog|critical" /var/log/syslog | tail -40' 2>&1
items.ai_logs_output: return BMC syslog config + remote rsyslog matches so user confirms critical Redfish/WebGUI content reached the remote syslog. No RISK (read-only).

items.criteria:
1. All logs (System Event logs, Security logs, SEL logs, OEM logs, POST logs) will be downloaded as a package.
2. Total duration won't over 10 minutes.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel list 2>&1; echo ---; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X GET https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices | jq
items.ai_logs_output: collect System Event + Security + SEL + OEM + POST logs via the commands shown and return them concatenated. No RISK.

items.criteria:
1. Reboot BMC without error.
2. BMC setting should not change after BMC back.
3. Check sensor list still can read data after BMC back. (user should check with RD how long will sensor ready)
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc reset cold 2>&1; sleep 90; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1
items.ai_logs_output: send `ipmitool mc reset cold` to reboot the BMC, wait, then `mc info` to confirm the BMC comes back without error and settings persist.
items.risk: RISK: state-changing: cold-resets the BMC, briefly dropping out-of-band management access (~1-2 min); confirm no in-flight OOB operations first.

-- This error means that the BMC client needs to verify that the LDAP server's certificate has been signed by a known CA. The service action would be for the admin to upload the CA certificate to the BMC.
-- To upload the CA certificate to the BMC, refer to the "Update LDAP root certificate" section of this document.
b) openbmctool doesn't support individual LDAP config property update, To update a single property user need to recreate the LDAP config with the changed values.

Agent runs it when the certificate is in place and verifies success.
items.ai_logs_output: return the openbmctool output + cert-upload status so the user confirms the Secure/ldaps LDAP config + cert uploaded (note: FQDN must match the cert to avoid hostname errors).
items.risk: RISK: enabling Secure LDAP with a wrong cert/FQDN can break BMC auth; supply the correct cert + FQDN.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Select "Hardware status" > Click tab "Inventory and LEDs" then check the system informatio

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: System data should be readable and correct.
items.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X GET https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems/system | jq {Model:.Model, Status:.Status}
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL pretty-printed JSON from /redfish/v1/Systems/system (System resource) so user can read/diff against SPEC for "System". No RISK (read-only).

    1. Send OEM command to set FAN speed : ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x01 0x64
    Fan PWM Duty Cycle:
       - 0x14 : 20%
       - 0x32 : 50%
       - 0x46 : 70%
       - 0x5A : 90%
       - 0x64 : 100%
2. Raise 5% , and then check FAN speed via SDR: ipmitool sdr elist
3. Check all FAN speed in chassis

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. When FAN speed percentage increase, FAN speed in SDR should also increase.
2. No FAN speed log when using manaul setting
items.ai_commands: -- Manually FAN speed control: set fan speed to a manual value ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" raw 0x30 0x30 0x01 0x00 0xAA 2>&1 / ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" raw 0x30 0x30 0x02 0xff {duty} 2>&1; sleep 5; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sensor list 2>&1 | grep -iE "FAN|SPD"; state-changing fan-speed override.
items.ai_logs_output: return the set-raw response + the fan RPM sensor read so the user confirms the manual duty changed the fan actual speed.
items.risk: RISK: locking a manual fan duty can overheat the system; set a safe duty, and restore auto mode after.

        56h = Self Test function not implemented in this controller

        For byte 2 = 58h, all other: Device-specific
        For byte 2 = 57h: self-test error bitfield. Note: returning 57h does not imply that all tests were run, just that a given test has failed. (i.e. 1b means failed, 0b means unknown.)
        [7] 1b = Cannot access SEL device
        [6] 1b = Cannot access SDR Repository
        [5] 1b = Cannot access BMC FRU device
        [4] 1b = IPMB signal lines do not respond
        [3] 1b = SDR Repository empty
        [2] 1b = Internal Use Area of BMC FRU corrupted
        [1] 1b = controller update boot block firmware corrupted

    【During Test】
    1. Establish an SOL session:
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> sol activate
2. Get payload instance info:
    Send in-band command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 in localhost.
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 from a remote client.
    Copy the response data (ex. 01 3b 00 02) to the command of "Get Session Info"
    Send command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x3d 0xff <response data of get payload instance info>.
3. Deactivate the SOL session:
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> sol deactivate
4. Get payload instance info again:
    Send in-band command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 in localhost.
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 from a remote client.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

    【During Test】
    Set boot flags:
    - For one-time boot:
      Send in-band command in localhost:
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0x80 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (Legacy mode)
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xa0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (uEFI mode)
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0 0
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x04 0xff 0x00
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x03 0x1f
    - Persistent for all future boots (requests BIOS to change its boot settings):
      Send in-band command in localhost:
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xc0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (Legacy mode)
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xe0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (uEFI mode)
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0 0
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x04 0xff 0x00
          ipmitool raw 0x00 0x08 0x03 0x1f
      Boot device:
         - 0x04 : PXE
         - 0x08 : Local default hard drive
         - 0x14 : default CD/DVD

1970. For example, 1440161475.
Convert it to a readable format by Linux command: date -d @1440161475.
And the result would be like: Fri Aug 21 20:51:15 CST 2015.

    【During Test】
    1. Check FRU Inventory Offset:
    Send command: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x10 0 and check byte 4 of the response data.
    If byte 4 is 00, then offset would be 0x00 0x00.
    If byte 4 if 01, then offset would be 0x01 0x00.

    Send in-band command: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x11 <Device ID> <Offset> <Count to read> in localhost.

    - Offset: 0x00 0x00 or 0x01 0x00. Depend on the result of step 1.
    - Count to read: Start from 0x01. Try to read as many as possible. For example, 0xf0.
    Check the response data.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

        56h = Self Test function not implemented in this controller
        57h = Corrupted or inaccessible data or devices

        For byte 2 = 55h, 56h, FFh: 00h
        For byte 2 = 58h, all other: Device-specific
        For byte 2 = 57h: self-test error bitfield. Note: returning 57h does not imply that all tests were run, just that a given test has failed. (i.e. 1b means failed, 0b means unknown.)
        [7] 1b = Cannot access SEL device
        [6] 1b = Cannot access SDR Repository
        [5] 1b = Cannot access BMC FRU device
        [4] 1b = IPMB signal lines do not respond
        [3] 1b = SDR Repository empty
        [2] 1b = Internal Use Area of BMC FRU corrupted
        [1] 1b = controller update boot block firmware corrupted
        [0] 1b = controller operational firmware corrupted

    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.

    【During Test】
    1. Establish an SOL session:
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> sol activate
2. Get payload instance info:
    Send in-band command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 in localhost.
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 from a remote client.
    Copy the response data (ex. 01 3b 00 02) to the command of "Get Session Info"
    Send command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x3d 0xff <response data of get payload instance info>.
3. Deactivate the SOL session:
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> sol deactivate
4. Get payload instance info again:
    Send in-band command: ipmitool raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 in localhost.
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x06 0x4b 0x01 0x01 from a remote client.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Set boot flags:
    - For one-time boot:
      Send out-of-band command from a remote client:
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0x80 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (Legacy mode)
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xa0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (uEFI mode)
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0 0
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x04 0xff 0x00
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x03 0x1f
    - Persistent for all future boots (requests BIOS to change its boot settings):
      Send out-of-band command from a remote client:
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xc0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (Legacy mode)
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x05 0xe0 <Boot device> 0 0 0 (uEFI mode)
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0 0
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x04 0xff 0x00
          ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x00 0x08 0x03 0x1f
      Boot device:
         - 0x04 : PXE
         - 0x08 : Local default hard drive
         - 0x14 : default CD/DVD
         - 0x18 : BIOS setup menu
         - 0x3c : Primary removable media (USB)
4. Restart SUT and check if it could boot into the right boot option. (within 60 seconds.)
5. Check boot option in BIOS.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Commands should be sent without any error.
2. SUT should boot into the correct boot option as setting.
3. Boot option should be correct as setting.
items.ai_commands: -- not directly runnable with stock ipmitool high-level (Set System Boot Options); give exact bytes.
items.ai_logs_output: none.
items.risk: RISK: chassis-related write - user request only.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x04 0x02 <Request data> from a remote client.
Request data (Use "Get SEL Entry" command to check the event record for the request data):
    Byte 1 : EvMRev (Byte 13 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 2 : Sensor Type (Byte 14 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 3 : Sensor # (Byte 15 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 4 : Event Dir | Event Type (Byte 16 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 5 : Event Data 1 (Byte 17 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 6 : Event Data 2 (Byte 18 of Get SEL Entry response data)
    Byte 7 : Event Data 3 (Byte 19 of Get SEL Entry response data)

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.

items.ai_logs_output: return the Platform Event (0x04 0x02) response so the user confirms it was accepted without error.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Clear SEL:
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x0a 0x47 <Reserve ID> 0x43 0x4c 0x52 0xaa from a remote client.
    Check the response data.
Get erasure status:
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x0a 0x47 <Reserve ID> 0x43 0x4c 0x52 0 from a remote client.
    Check the response data.
 - Reserve ID : Use "ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x42" to get the reserve ID.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Commands should be sent without any error.
2. Response data should be 01 that means erase completed. 00 means erasure in progress.
3. Sending "Get Erasure Status" should NOT clear SEL if SEL list is not empty.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel clear
items.ai_logs_output: return `sel clear` confirmation; verify SEL is now empty via `sel list`.
items.risk: RISK: ERASES the system event log - run only on user explicit request, never auto-run.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x0a 0x48 from a remote client.
Check the response data. (LS byte first)
For example, c3 1e d7 55.
Convert the response data to decimal by Linux command: echo $((16#55d71ec3))
It will change to a value which is the local time as the number of seconds from 00:00:00, January 1,
1970. For example, 1440161475.
Convert it to a readable format by Linux command: date -d @1440161475.
And the result would be like: Fri Aug 21 20:51:15 CST 2015.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.

items.ai_logs_output: return FULL raw `ipmitool sel ...` output; user checks SEL entries / time expected.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x0a 0x49 <Timestamp format> from a remote client.
Timestamp format:
    Use Linux command: date +%s to show the valuewhich is the local time as the number of seconds from 00:00:00, January 1, 1970. For example, 1440161475.
    Convert the number to hexadecimal. For example, 55d71ec3.
    Split the number to 4 parts and record them with LS byte first. For example, c3 1e d7 55.
So an example to set SEL time would be like: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x49 0xc3 0x1e 0xd7 0x55.
Send command of "Get SEL Time" and check the result.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Command should be sent without any error.
2. The time should be set correctly.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sel time set
items.ai_logs_output: return `sel time set` output; verify via `sel time get`.
items.risk: RISK: changes SEL time - user request only.

    1. Check FRU Inventory Offset:
    Send command: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x10 0 and check byte 4 of the response data.
    If byte 4 is 00, then offset would be 0x00 0x00.

2. Read FRU Data:
    Send out-of-band command: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> raw 0x0a 0x11 <Device ID> <Offset> <Count to read> from a remote client.
    - Device ID: send command "ipmitool fru" to check available IDs. For example, ID 0 = 0x00.
    - Offset: 0x00 0x00 or 0x01 0x00. Depend on the result of step 1.
    - Count to read: Start from 0x01. Try to read as many as possible. For example, 0xf0.
    Check the response data.

    【After Test】

    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.ai_commands:
BASE="https://${BMC_IP:?from 6969 /api/machines/{name}.bmc_ip}/redfish/v1"
AUTH="${BMC_USER:?from 6969}:${BMC_PASS:?from 6969}"
# 1) 拿 System id (真路徑: /redfish/v1/Systems/<id>, 如 11.RestAPI/System/system.txt 的 "system")
SYS=$(curl -s -k -u "$AUTH" "$BASE/Systems/Members" | jq -r '.Members[0]."@odata.id"' | xargs basename)
echo "=== System id: $SYS (以該機 BMC SPEC 為準) ==="
echo "=== Processors collection ==="
curl -s -k -u "$AUTH" "$BASE/Systems/$SYS/Processors" | jq .
echo "=== Each processor detail ==="
for m in $(curl -s -k -u "$AUTH" "$BASE/Systems/$SYS/Processors" | jq -r '.Members[]."@odata.id"'); do
  echo "--- $m ---"
  curl -s -k -u "$AUTH" "$m" | jq '.ProcessorType,.PartNumber,.Manufacturer,.Model,.Id,.Status'
done 2>&1 | tee /var/log/Wistron-BMC-00618-V004_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log
items.ai_logs_output: return the Processors collection + each processor instance (Id/ProcessorType/PartNumber/Manufacturer/Model/Status) so the operator confirms CPU details are readable via Redfish. BMC IP/帳密來源: 6969 /api/machines/{name} (bmc_ip/bmc_user/bmc_pass). TLS 跳驗證(BMC 自簽). 路徑依 11.RestAPI: /redfish/v1/Systems/<id>/Processors. Log saved to: /var/log/Wistron-BMC-00618-V004_<ts>.log.

items.ai_commands:
-- POST Update BMC Firmware (Wistron real path = HttpPushUri; see data/11+12.RestAPI/BMC update).
  RUN ON AGENT HOST (no ssh; the BMC image lives locally).

  # 1) resolve the HttpPushUri endpoint (Wistron BMC)
  URI=$(curl -sk -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/UpdateService" | jq -r '.HttpPushUri')

  # 2) upload the operator-supplied image
  curl -sk -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" -X POST \
      -T "${BMC_IMAGE:?operator must provide the BMC firmware image path on the agent host}" \
      "https://$BMC_IP$URI"

  # 3) optional: trigger apply immediately (see data/11.RestAPI/BMC update; operator consent + standby machine)
  curl -sk -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PATCH \
      -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime":"Immediate"}}}' \

    【During Test】

items.criteria:
1. BMC LAN should be functional after FW flash stress.
2. BMC SEL and OS event log should NOT have any error message about stress
items.ai_packages_needed: BMC FW images 1 and 2 (user-designated) + BMC firmware-update tool (web/REDFISH UpdateService)
items.ai_commands: -- BMC Firmware Flash cycle: upgrade/downgrade BMC FW image 1 and 2 in a loop 500x while checking BMC LAN stays functional. State-changing + very long; the flash command needs the user-designated .ima images and a full uninterrupted loop - agent stages it and verifies LAN per iteration, pending approval of the 500-cycle runtime.
items.ai_logs_output: return per-iteration flash status + a LAN ping/SEL check (e.g. sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ping -c1 $BMC_IP 2>&1; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -20 2>&1") so the user confirms BMC LAN stayed functional with no error SEL after the stress.
items.risk: RISK: 500 BMC FW flash cycles can brick the BMC if any flash is interrupted; run only on a dedicated BMC with user-provided recovery images and do not power-cut mid-flash.

items.ai_commands: -- BMC FW Recovery: recover the BMC from a forced corrupt/empty state using the recovery image/RoP (Recovery of Last Resort) mechanism; must be staged offline or via the BMC recovery flow with the BMC image. This is a multi-step recovery, not a one-liner; sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "echo "place image + run recovery flow"; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" mc info 2>&1 | head -20 2>&1".  [scenario: BMC-RoT]
items.ai_logs_output: return the recovery flow output + the post-recovery BMC version so the user confirms the BMC came back from the forced-bad state. (context: BMC-RoT)

items.items: CPU over temperature via peltier device / remove heatsink
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Setup the system to a standard supported configuration.
2. Boot to OS.
3. Remove the Heat sink or Use a Peltier Device to slowly heat the CPU indicated under Configurations to the TWarning Threshold (Monitor the temperature increase via BMC web interface)
4. Once TWarning Threshold is reached, slowly proceed to add heat until TCritical threshold is reached.   (NOTE:  If you go too fast you may only trip the TCritical Threshold)
5. Continue Heating until system resets

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. System will shutdown once TCritical Threshold has been reached
2. BMC error log will show an over-temperature condition has been detected on CPUx
3. Temperature LED will light if there is one on the Diagnostic Panel
4. If there is a LCD Panel (Aria),  CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
5. Corresponding CPU lightpath will light
6. Front Panel Fault Light will Light
7. Once all checks are complete in during run time, reboot the system and check the uEFI SEL to ensure the corresponding log for CPU Over Temp was logged properly as well as the system reset
items.ai_commands: -- CPU over temperature via peltier device / remove heatsink: physically remove or heat the CPU heatsink with a peltier device to drive TCritical and verify shutdown + SEL over-temp entry. A physical/environmental fault-injection the agent cannot perform.
items.ai_logs_output: operator heats the CPU / removes the heatsink to reach TCritical, confirms shutdown, SEL over-temp entry and LED; agent cannot inject over-temp.

items.ai_commands:
-- Reboot 5 times: perform 5 OOB power cycles, confirming each reboot reaches the OS.
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power cycle 2>&1
  sleep 60
  sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "echo 'reboot $i'; uptime 2>&1" 2>&1
done
items.ai_logs_output: return the 5 reboot cycle markers + each boot uptime so the user confirms every reboot completed and booted to the OS cleanly.
items.risk: RISK: repeated reboots interrupt the host; run in a maintenance window.

3

items.ai_commands:

【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1.Use amd-smi for further read out of temperature, power, gfxclk frequency with the following
command:
$ amd-smi monitor -w 5
2. Execute the following command on separate terminal:
$ ./agt -i=0,5,10,15,20,25,30,35 -unilog=PM -unilogallgroups -unilogperiod=50 -clkrestore -unilogoutput=pm_xxx.csv
Description: Use AGT tool to collect unilog for all GPU. The log samples every 50ms indicated with -
unilogperiod. Below information will be available in the log located in AGT run directory.
Timestamp, All-related GPU infrastructure power readings, All-related GPU clock frequency, GPU
XGMI Read Write bandwidth, Etc.
3. Start system logging. Poll, monitor and collect: Ambient Inlet Temperature, System Fan Speeds,
Power Supply Output Power. Note that these commands may vary across systems, and there may
be more efficient proprietary means of logging these sensors individually on a given system. Collect
these data from Redfish.
4. Allow the system (GPUs and CPUs) to Idle for a minimum of one (1) minute to allow temperatures
to drop, GPU GFXCLKs to dynamically drop to lower states, System Fan speeds to drop, and Power
Supply loads to drop. This period will allow us to synchronize data more easily between the disparate GPU logs, system logs, and DGEMM output logs. If the fan speed does not drop within this window, you may need to increase the idle time for this step accordingly and restart the test.
5. Coralgemm
Run the Coralgemm workload on a single GPU for 900 seconds. Change the ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES value according to each GPU from 0 to 7. Capture the output logs showing GFLOP performance per DGEMM run within the looped test.
$ ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 900 strided 
6. Allow the system (GPUs and CPUs) to Idle for a minimum of one (1) minute to allow temperatures to drop, GPU GFXCLKs to dynamically drop to lower states, System Fan speeds to drop, and Power Supply loads to drop. This period will serve as the second book-end to allow us to synchronize data more easily between the disparate GPU logs, system logs, and DGEMM output logs, especially when they may have different sampling periods
>> sleep 60
7. Repeat steps 5 and 6 for the remaining GPUs individually by using the following:
– ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 #GPU 1
– ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 #GPU 2
– ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 #GPU 3
– ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES from 0 to 7.
8. Complete the test. Stop all logging and collect all log files. Retrieve and clean the system logs for any GPU-reported errors.

【After Test】 
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.test_set: Advanced - Serial Port Console Redirection - Enable & Disabled
items.items: Serial Port Console Redirection - Enable & Disabled
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BIOS -> Advanced -> Serial Port Console Redirection
2. Set "Console Redirection" to Disabled, and then save & exit.
3. Reboot SUT and check that COM port terminal should NOT display boot progress.
4.Enter BIOS -> Advanced -> Serial Port Console Redirection
5. Set "Console Redirection" to Enabled, and then save & exit.
6. Reboot SUT and check that COM port terminal should display boot progress.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. When "Console Redirection" is set to Disabled,  COM port terminal should NOT display boot progress while reboot SUT.
2. When "Console Redirection" is set to Enabled,  COM port terminal should display boot progress while reboot SUT.
items.ai_commands: -- Serial Port Console Redirection - Enable & Disabled: toggling Serial Port Console Redirection in the BIOS Advanced page changes the serial console behaviour; both the BIOS setting change and the serial redirection observation need a person at the console.
items.ai_logs_output: operator toggles the setting and verifies serial redirection; agent cannot drive the BIOS UI or a physical serial console.

items.items: Check BMC version from BIOS / ipmi / BMC Web / redfish
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check BMC version in BIOS Server Mgmt page.
2. Check BMC verision in OS via cmd: 
IB: ipmitool mc info
OOB: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H <BMC IP> -U root -P 0penBmc mc info
3. Check BMC verision in BMC-Web.
4. redfish command: curl -s -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@<BMC IP>/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: 1. All BMC versions should be correct.
items.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -iE "firmware"; echo ---; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X GET https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc | jq .FirmwareVersion
items.ai_logs_output: return BMC firmware version from both `ipmitool mc info` and Redfish so user confirms they match. No RISK.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Settings -> Network.
2. Add static IPv4 addresses & static DNS on all BMC ports, and then ping their Static-IPs.
3. Delete static IPv4 addresses & static DNS on all BMC ports.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Add static IPv4 addresses & static DNS on all BMC ports without errors, and ping their BMC-IPs successfully.
1. Delete static IPv4 addresses & static DNS on all BMC ports without errors.
items.ai_commands: -- Network: add static IPv4 + static DNS on all BMC ports (web -> Settings -> Network), ping each static IP, then delete them. Adding/configuring is a BMC-web/Redfish action; agent verifies the addresses are up (ping) and that deletion clears them, via curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces" 2>&1 | jq -r ".Members[].Id" 2>&1; ping -c1 $BMC_IP 2>&1.
items.ai_logs_output: return the per-port static IPv4/DNS add + ping result + the post-delete interface list so the user confirms static add/delete on all BMC ports worked without errors.
items.risk: RISK: adding a wrong static IP/DNS can break BMC management; use valid address/DNS and keep a console path.

    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Settings -> Power restore policy.
2. Set power restore policy to "Always on", and then click "Save settings".
3. AC off & on SUT.
4. Check that SUT should automatically power on.
5. Swap CPU then check power on behavior.

    【After Test】

    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. When power restore policy is set to "Always on", SUT should automatically power on after AC off & on.
2. After swap CPU, the SUT should be power on successful
3.After swap CPU, the SUT should be power on successful
(Updated steps & Criteria by issue [DarkStar] System always reboot automatically in early post DXE core stage after swap Genoa CPU9654  to Genoa CPU9554.)
items.ai_commands: -- Power Restore Policy - Always on: agent can read/set the power restore policy via Redfish curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems/system 2>&1 | grep -i powerrestore 2>&1 but the AC-cord unplug/replug + verifying the SUT powers on/off accordingly requires a person at the PDU/AC. Agent sets policy and reads it back; the AC behavior check is operator.
items.ai_logs_output: return the Redfish PowerRestorePolicy value set+read back so the user confirms it persisted; the AC unplug/replug power-restore behavior is operator-observed.
items.risk: RISK: setting power-restore policy is state-changing; AC unplug/replug must be done by a person, never hot-pull power on a running service.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

【During Test】
A.Install and Configure Apache HTTP Server
1.Install Apache HTTP Server
sudo apt update
sudo apt install apache2
sudo systemctl start apache2
sudo systemctl enable apache2

2.Generate SSL Certificate
sudo mkdir /etc/apache2/certs
sudo openssl genrsa -out /etc/apache2/certs/server.key 2048
sudo openssl req -new -x509 -key /etc/apache2/certs/server.key -out /etc/apache2/certs/server.crt -days 365 -subj "/C=US/ST=State/L=City/O=Organization/CN=your server IP"

3.Configure Apache to use HTTPS
sudo a2enmod ssl

4.Edit the configuration file and add the following content:
vi /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf
#----------------------------------
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    Redirect permanent / https://yourdomain.com/
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/apache2/certs/server.crt
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/apache2/certs/server.key
</VirtualHost>
#----------------------------------

5.Restart Apache
sudo systemctl restart apache2



B.Upload Http certificate
1.Generate CSR file
BMC web > Security and access > Certificates > Generate CSR
Certificate type = HTTPS Certificate
Country/Region = Taiwan
State = None
City = Taipei
Company name = Wistron
Company unit = PV
Common name (CN) = Server IP
Private key = RAS
Key bit length = 2048
 
2.Copy CSR file to Server 
3.Generate Client Certificate
openssl x509 -req -in /path/to/CSR_File.csr -CA /path/to/Server_CA.crt -CAkey /path/to/Server_CA.key -CAcreateserial -out /path/to/Client.crt -days 365 -sha256
4.Check Client.crt file
openssl x509 -in “/path/to/Client.crt” -text -noout
5.Copy Client.crt to client system.
6.Get crt and copy content
sed -E ':a;N;$!ba;s/\r{0,1}\n/\\n/g' Client.crt 
7.Create Json file and add the following content
vi certificate.json
#----------------------------------
{
    "CertificateString": "{You copy the contents of Client.crt}",
    "CertificateType": "PEM",
    "CertificateUri":
    {
        "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol/HTTPS/Certificates/1"
}
}
#----------------------------------
8.Get Client BMC token
curl -k -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST https://{Client_BMC_IP}/login -d '{"username" : "root", "password" : "0penBmc"}'
Ex."token": "SQt7hY3umbIYmer3sAib"
9.Update the HTTP certificate using the following command to complete the certificate update.
curl -c cjar -b cjar -k -H "X-Auth-Token: {token}" -X POST https://{Client_BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/CertificateService/Actions/CertificateService.ReplaceCertificate/ -d @certificate.json

【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
items.criteria:
1.Generate CSR without errors.
2.Check the BMC Web Certificates to see if they have been updated.
3.Certificates information should be correct.
4.Upload the HTTPS certificate without any errors.

    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Hardware Status -> Inventory and LEDs.
2. Check "Fans" information.

    【After Test】

items.criteria: 1. All information should match SPEC definition.
