items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check power policy again: ipmitool chassis status
2. When SUT is power on, unplug AC power cord and replug the power cord. Check SUT power status.
3. When SUT is power off, unplug AC power cord and replug the power cord. Check SUT power status.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Power Restore Policy of "ipmitool chassis status" should be as setting.
2. SUT power restore behavior should be correct as setting.
    - SUT should be power on after AC power back when previous state is power on.
    - SUT should be power off after AC power back when previous state is power off.
items.ai_commands: -- Power Policy - Check default policy: read the default AC power-loss policy ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" raw 0x30 0x42 0x06 0x02 0x01 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" chassis status 2>&1 | grep -i -E "Power Restore|Power Restore Policy" and redfish curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems/system" 2>&1 | jq -r ".PowerRestorePolicy" 2>&1.
items.ai_logs_output: return the raw/redfish power-policy value so the user confirms the default policy (power on/off/last state) is as spec.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set to always-off: ipmitool chassis policy always-off
2. Check policy setting: ipmitool chassis status
3. Run BMC cold reset: ipmitool mc reset cold
4. Check power policy again: ipmitool chassis status
5. When SUT is power on/off, unplug AC power cord and replug the power cord. Check SUT power status.
6. Swap CPU then check power on behavior.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Power Restore Policy of "ipmitool chassis status" should be as setting.
2. SUT power restore behavior should be correct as setting.
    - Alwats power off -> SUT should always remain off even after AC power back.
3.After swap CPU, the SUT should be power on successful
(Updated steps & Criteria by issue [DarkStar] System always reboot automatically in early post DXE core stage after swap Genoa CPU9654  to Genoa CPU9554.)
items.ai_commands:
-- Power Policy - Always power off: set the AC power-loss policy to always-off (OOB chassis policy), verify, then note the physical AC-cycle step needs the operator.
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis policy always-off 2>&1
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis status 2>&1 | grep -iE 'Power Restore'
-- state-changing; the AC unplug/replug + swap-CPU steps are operator-physical (agent cannot cycle AC/swap CPU).
items.ai_logs_output: return the set response + policy readback + the observed power state after AC restore so the user confirms Last-State behaviour.
items.risk: RISK: Last-State restores whatever state was present at power loss; restore the intended policy after the test.

items.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to Disk
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    I. Pre-check in BIOS:
1. Advanced -> Redfish Host Interface Settings -> Redfish [Enabled]
2. Advanced -> Network Stack [Enabled]
3. Advanced -> Network Stack -> IPv4 PXE Support [Enabled]
4. Advanced -> Network Stack -> IPv4 HTTP Support [Enabled]

II. Set boot option in OS:
1. Set boot option: ipmitool chassis bootdev disk options=efiboot
2. Check boot option: ipmitool chassis bootparam get 5
3. Restart the node and check if it could boot into Disk.
4. Check boot option in BIOS.
Note: Please note BMC will aotomatically clear the boot flag in about 60 sec ( +-10% )

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Node should boot into Disk.
2. Boot option should be correct as setting.
items.ai_packages_needed: curl + BMC creds; the boot target must exist (media/disk/PXE server)
items.ai_commands: -- Boot Order - Set boot option to Disk: set the boot option to Disk via Redfish PATCH /redfish/v1/Systems/system with BootSourceOverrideEnabled=Once + BootSourceOverrideTarget=<Disk>. State-changing; agent sends the PATCH curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PATCH -d '{"Boot":{"BootSourceOverrideTarget":"Hdd","BootSourceOverrideEnabled":"Once"}}' "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems/system" 2>&1 then reboots and confirms the host booted from Disk (or that future-boot persisted).
items.ai_logs_output: return the PATCH response + post-reboot boot order/status (ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" chassis bootparam get 5 2>&1) so the user confirms the node booted into Disk and the boot option is correct; for the next boot only.
items.risk: RISK: setting the boot target changes what the node boots; confirm the target media is ready and restore the normal boot order after the check.

items.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to Virtual ISO
items.procedure:

-- Boot Order - Set boot option to BIOS: set the one-time boot option to BIOS Setup via IPMI, reboot, and confirm the host enters BIOS.

items.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to BIOS for all future-boot
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    I. Pre-check in BIOS:
1. Advanced -> Redfish Host Interface Settings -> Redfish [Enabled]
2. Advanced -> Network Stack [Disabled]

II. Set boot option in OS:
1. Set boot option: ipmitool chassis bootdev bios options=efiboot,persistent
2. Check boot option: ipmitool chassis bootparam get 5
3. Restart the node and check if it could boot into BIOS.
4. Restart the node again and check if it could boot into BIOS persistently for all future-boot.
Note: Please note BMC will aotomatically clear the boot flag in about 60 sec ( +-10% )

III. Recover boot option:
ipmitool chassis bootdev none options=persistent

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Node should boot into BIOS.
2. Boot option should be correct as setting.
3. While Persistent Boot Order is enabled via BMC, POST message should display a message that the persistent boot order is set.
items.ai_packages_needed: curl + BMC creds; the boot target must exist (media/disk/PXE server)
items.ai_commands:
-- Boot Order - Set boot option to BIOS for all future-boot: set a persistent boot option to BIOS Setup via IPMI, reboot twice, and confirm it persists.
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis bootdev setup options=efiboot,persistent 2>&1
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis bootparam get 5 2>&1
-- state-changing/pre-OS; agent reads back the boot option; entering BIOS + the persistent-boot POST message is operator-visual.
items.ai_logs_output: return the PATCH response + post-reboot boot order/status (ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" chassis bootparam get 5 2>&1) so the user confirms the node booted into BIOS and the boot option is correct; for all future-boot.

items.ai_commands: -- Hard Reset stress runs the BMC-initiated operation repeatedly for 24h. Agent can run one shot now for a sanity pass: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" power reset 2>&1, but the full 24h loop needs a scripted loop + a maintenance window + confirmation the DUT stays reachable after each cycle.
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL ipmitool result for one Hard Reset cycle + then a looped run (e.g. for i in $(seq 1 N); do ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" power reset; sleep 60; done) so the user confirms no fail over the stress duration; 24h duration is user-approved.
items.risk: RISK: repeated power reset/cold-reset drops the host repeatedly over 24h; only on a dedicated/ready DUT with a maintenance window and remote-recovery in place.

items.items: Configuring BMC Network through IPMI for static(IB)
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set IP address source command:
Send in-band command: ipmitool lan set <channel> ipsrc <source>
Channel: 
 eth0 = 1
 eth1 = 2
source:
 static = address manually configured to be static
 dhcp = address obtained by BMC running DHCP

2. Set channel IP addresss command:
ipmitool lan set <channel> ipaddr <x.x.x.x>

3. Set channel IP netmask command:
ipmitool lan set <channel> netmask <x.x.x.x>

4. Set channel IP gateway:
ipmitool lan set <channel> defgw ipaddr <x.x.x.x>

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Commands should be sent without any error.
2. The response datas should be correct as the output of ipmitool lan print.
items.ai_commands: -- Configuring BMC Network through IPMI for static(IB): set the BMC network to a static IP (IB) via IPMI ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 ipsrc static 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 ipaddr 192.168.0.50 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 netmask 255.255.255.0 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|Subnet Mask|IP Source"; state-changing network setting.
items.ai_logs_output: return the final `ipmitool lan print` (ip source = static + the new IP/netmask) so the user confirms the BMC static IP was applied.
items.risk: RISK: changing the BMC IP drops the current out-of-band channel; keep a console/serial path and restore the original IP after.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    I. Set FAN speed with full FAN:
1. Check FAN speed via SDR: ipmitool sdr elist
2. Set FAN speed to 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% in sequence: 
a. Set FAN speed: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x01 <PWM>
    <PWM>
    - 20%: 0x14
    - 25%: 0x19
    - 50%: 0x32
    - 70%: 0x46
    - 75%: 0x4b
    - 90%: 0x5A
    - 100%: 0x64
b. Check FAN speed via SDR: ipmitool sdr elist
c. Check FAN speed via cmd: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x22
3. Recover FAN to Auto-Control: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x00

II. Re-install FAN after setting FAN speed:
1. Set all FAN speed to 75%: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x01 0x4b
2. Check FAN speed via SDR: ipmitool sdr elist
3. Check FAN speed via cmd: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x22
4. Plug-out 1 of FAN, and then re-install it.
5. Check FAN speed via SDR: ipmitool sdr elist
6. Check FAN speed via cmd: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x22
7. Recover FAN to Auto-Control: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x00

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Set FAN speed without errors, and the reading of FAN should be correct.
2. Recover FAN to Auto-Control successfully.

    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Clear SEL: ipmitool sel clear
2. Check that there should be no SEL-log: ipmitool sel elist
3. Add SEL Entry for 3 times: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x44 0x01 0 0x02 0x01 0x01 0x01 0x01 0x20 0 0x04 0x32 0x40 0x81 0x0b 0 0
　※Note: Run cmd for 3 times
 
4.Check that 3 SEL Entry should be generated: ipmitool sel elist
5.Get the reserve ID: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x42
　※Note: For example, get response data: c9 1a

6. Delete No.2 SEL Entry: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x46 0xc9 0x1a 0x2 0

7.Check that No.2 SEL Entry should be deleted: ipmitool sel elist
8.Get the new reserve ID: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x42
　※Note: For example, get response data: df 6b

9. Before clear all SEL Entry, get erasure status: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x47 0xdf 0x6b 0x43 0x4c 0x52 0

10.Clear all SEL Entry: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x47 0xdf 0x6b 0x43 0x4c 0x52 0xaa
11.Check that all SEL Entry should be cleared: ipmitool sel elist

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.ai_commands:
-- FAN speed change(Auto): idle then load the SUT and snapshot fan RPM + power via OOB (agent-host); fan response is read-only.
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "stress-ng --cpu \$(nproc) --timeout 30 2>&1 | tail -3" &
sleep 5
echo '---fan_idle---'
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'fan'
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'power' | head
wait
echo '---post---'
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'fan'
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL fan-RPM snapshots recording fan RPM + power consumption under auto control as load changes (before + after a load/duty change) so the user confirms fan speed responds as expected.

echo '---restore---'
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" raw 0x30 0x81 0x1 0xf8 0x0 0x24 0x32 2>&1

items.ai_commands:
-- Cold Reboot: cold-reboot stress - record lspci/lsblk/nvme on the DUT, then power off/on via OOB (agent-host), looped for the long-term count.
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci -vv > /tmp/cold_lspci.txt; lsblk > /tmp/cold_lsblk.txt; nvme list > /tmp/cold_nvme.txt 2>&1; echo recorded" 2>&1

sleep 30
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power on 2>&1

1. Send command: badblocks -sv -b 4096 /dev/sdx

items.items: BMC Stress - Masses of BMC Load
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Keep sending IPMI OOB commands and IB commands (ex. ipmitool mc info, ipmitool sel elist, ipmitool sdr elist), and keep showing OS event log via cmd "dmesg" for 12 hours.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. BMC should be functional after stress.
2. BMC SEL and OS event log should NOT have any error message because of stress.
items.ai_commands: -- BMC Stress sends a high volume of IPMI OOB+IB commands repeatedly. Agent can run a burst loop: for i in $(seq 1 N); do ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 >/dev/null; done; capture latency/errors. The mass-load soak is user-scheduled.
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL loop timing/error summary (e.g. time for N get-device-id + any failures) so the user confirms the BMC handles sustained load without dropping.
items.risk: RISK: sustained high-volume BMC traffic stresses the management channel; use an OOB-dedicated channel and avoid flooding the production LAN.

-- I2C MB: enumerate and scan the motherboard I2C segment (read-only).
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "echo ---i2c_buses---; sudo i2cdetect -l 2>&1; echo ---scan---; for b in \$(sudo i2cdetect -l 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'i2c-[0-9]+' | cut -d- -f2); do sudo i2cdetect -y \$b 2>/dev/null | head -20; done" 2>&1
items.ai_logs_output: return FULL `i2cdetect -l` bus list + per-bus `i2cdetect -y <bus>` scan so the user confirms the motherboard I2C segment is enumerated and addressable per the spec. No RISK (read-only bus scan).

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

【During Test】 
1. Check SDR-List via IB & OOB cmd:
$ ipmitool sdr elist 
$ ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H <BMC_IP> -U <BMC_User> -P <BMC_Password> sdr elist 

2. Check Sensor-List via IB & OOB cmd:
$ ipmitool sensor list |grep TEMP_UBB_GPU0~7M (For AMDGPU)
$ ipmitool sensor list |grep TEMP_GB_GPU1~8_M(For NVGPU)
$ ipmitool -I lanplus-C 17 -H <BMC_IP> -U <BMC_User> -P <BMC_Password> sensor list | grep TEMP_UBB_GPU0~7M or TEMP_GB_GPU1~8_M

3. Check BMC web > Sensor list

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr type 'Power Supply' 2>&1; echo ---PSU-SDR---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'PSU|STATUS' | head -n 40
items.ai_logs_output: return the PSU SDR rows so the operator confirms names/descriptions/readings match the SPEC SDR + sensor lists.

items.procedure: 100x Warm reboots, check for reliable power control and ensure OS, PCIe, MCTP, SSIF and FPGA stability each cycle
items.criteria:
Ensure reliable OS boot and constant PCIe and MCTP enumeration and FPGA stability

NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 System Validation Guide (NVOnline: TBD)
items.ai_commands: for i in $(seq 1 5); do ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power cycle; sleep 240; ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "$DUT_USER@$DUT_IP" "echo cycle=$i; uptime; dmesg | grep -ciE 'AER'"; done
items.ai_logs_output: run a shortened warm-reboot stress loop (the spec requires 100x; agent runs a representative sub-set and reports counts of AER/dmesg hits per cycle; full 100x is time-prohibitive to automate).
items.risk: RISK: destructive/long: repeated power cycles reboots the SUT many times and interrupts all running state; full 100x takes hours. Agent runs a reduced loop for smoke evidence; the full 100x count is best left to a scheduled operator/bench run.

items.procedure: 100x AC cycles by completely removing power from tray, check for reliable power control and ensure OS, PCIe, MCTP, SSIF and FPGA stability each cycle
items.criteria:
Ensure reliable OS boot and constant PCIe and MCTP enumeration and SMA stability

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 System Validation Guide (NVOnline: TBD)
items.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this "AC reboot stress" (100x) requires physically removing AC power from the tray repeatedly and restoring it; the agent cannot physically operate the AC connector 100 times, and repeated full AC cycles are a destructive bench procedure.
items.ai_logs_output: operator performs the 100x AC-cycle bench procedure and records PCIe/MCTP/SMA stability; agent cannot automate physical AC removal.

items.procedure: 100x DC cycles (run power and standby power from BMC), check for reliable power control and ensure OS, PCIe, MCTP, SSIF and SMA stability each cycle
items.criteria:

items.procedure: Check inventory (FRU list) of every node in chassis

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1. SSH into BMC console and execute command to check current error injection mode.
$ curl -k http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_0 | grep -B 2 -A 1 EINJState
2. SSH into BMC console and execute the comand to enable error injection mode if EINJState is Disabled:
# curl -k -X POST http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_0/Actions/Oem/AMD/Chassis.ErrInjection -d
'{""ErrInjection"" : ""Enable""}' 
3. Repeat step 1 to check if EINJState changed to Pending to enable.
4. Reboot host or do a warm reset for changes to take effect.
5. Repeat step 1 to check if the EINJState changed to Enabled.

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: EINJState should be Enabled.
items.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish) on the BMC + BMC login; amdgpuras not strictly needed here
items.ai_commands:
-- RAS Enablement (AMD EINJState) via OOB Redfish from the agent host: read EINJState, and if disabled, enable it via the Redfish AMD ErrInjection action, then re-read.
curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_0 2>&1 | grep -i einjstate
-- enable (write; operator approves) then re-read EINJState above.
items.ai_logs_output: return the Redfish EINJState before/after so the user confirms Out-Of-Band RAS injection mode is Enabled.
items.risk: RISK: enabling OOB error-injection mode changes BMC config; leave it at the project-defined state after the test.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2. Execute the following command for getting card ID for all devices:
$ sudo amdgpuras -l | grep /dev/dri/card
3. Check the card ID by checking on the output
4. Execute the following command to list down current Retired Bad Page of device_id = 0:
$ cat /sys/class/drm/card<card_id>/device/ras/gpu_vram_bad_pages
5. Execute the following command for GFX poison consumption handling with ODECC injection to device_id = 0, block_id = 2 (GFX):
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 2 -t 8
6. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
7. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
8. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o ""<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper""
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp -o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper ""<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/""
9. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json
10. Repeat step 4 to check if the list of Bad Page Address increased.
11. Execute the following command to inject ODECC replay error at one of the addresses in the Bad
Page list from step 10:
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 0 -s 2 -t 4 -a 0x2fed1c0000

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
• PASS = 
- AMDGPURAS tool GFX error injection command returns Bus error.
- Redfish command for CPER index retrieval shows the CPER index is increased by 1 and new CPER file is generated upon the error injected.
- The decoded result from the decoded CPER log matches the injected error type and location.
• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: UMC.
• Errorcode ext is 0 and Errocode ext Type is On-die ECC.
• Error severity matches the type of error injected: Deferred error.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: GC.
• Errorcode ext is 62 and Errocode ext Type is GFX_IP_Poison_Error.
• Error severity matches the type of error injected: Uncorrected Error. Poison has been consumed.
• FAIL = 
- AMDGPU RAS Tool ODECC replay error injection command returns Failed.
items.ai_commands: -- Bad Page Avoidance (bad-page avoidance): clear RAS EEPROM, reload amdgpu with ras_enable=1, inject a GFX error via amdgpuras and confirm the CPER index increments + the bad page is avoided. Needs the exact amdgpuras inject command for this case.
items.ai_logs_output: return the amdgpuras injection result + the Redfish CPER index before/after + decoded CPER so the user confirms the bad page was avoided per spec.
items.risk: RISK: injecting a hardware/CPU error can disrupt the SUT and may need a reboot/recovery; run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact injection target confirmed by the user/FAE.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1. Execute the following command for clearing the RAS EEPROM:
$ for i in {0 .. 7}; do sudo amdgpuras -r -d $i; done
2. Reboot host or do warm reset for the RAS EEPROM clearance to take effect.
3. Load amdgpu driver by using the following command:
$ sudo modprobe amdgpu ras_enable=1
4. Execute the following command for getting card ID for all devices:
$ sudo amdgpuras -l | grep /dev/dri/card
5. Execute the following command to list down current Retired Bad Page of device_id = 0:
$ cat /sys/class/drm/card<card_id>/device/ras/gpu_vram_bad_pages
6. Execute the following command for GFX poison consumption handling with ODECC injection to
device_id = 0, block_id = 2 (GFX):
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 2 -t 8
7. Repeat step 5 to check if the list of Bad Page Address increased and record down the list to be compared later.
8. Perform an AC cycle
9. Repeat step 5 to check and compare the list of Bad Page Address and the recorded list in step 7.

OOB Check:
1. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '"Id": "[^"]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to check OOB event entries:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries'
3. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
4. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o "<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper"
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp –o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper "<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/"
5. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json

Inband Check:
1. Run the following command to dump inband cper from amdgpuras tool:
$ sudo amdgpuras -C

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
• PASS = 
- AMDGPURAS tool GFX error injection command returns Bus error.
- Redfish command for CPER index retrieval shows the CPER index is increased and new CPER file is generated upon the error injected.
- The decoded result from the decoded CPER log matches the injected error type and location.
• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: UMC.
• Errorcode ext is 0 and Errocode ext Type is On-die ECC.
• Error severity matches the type of error injected: Deferred error.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: GC.
• Errorcode ext is 62 and Errocode ext Type is GfxGcError.
• Error severity matches the type of error injected: Uncorrected Error. Poison
has been consumed.
- The list of retired bad page addresses remains the same as the list prior to AC cycle.
- The inband CPER log matches the OAM devices and error severity level

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

【During Test】
1. Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to query the UBB FW information, listing all FW components.
Example: ~ # curl -k -X GET htpp://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory
2.Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/retimer_active
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to query UBB FW Information for retimer_active.
Example:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/retimer_active
3. Repeat step 2 to query the Version for Bundle, IFWI, SMC, SMC_FPGA, Retimer, RMI, ROT, and UBB_FPGA. These versions must match the BKC release notes of BKC flashed. 
4. Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -H ""Content-type: application/octet-stream"" -X POST -T /<file_location>/bundle_name.pldm> http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to update UBB FW.
Example: ~ # curl -k -H ""Content-type: application/octet-stream"" -X POST -T ./BKC_B24.10.03.04_Debug.pldm http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService
5. Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/0
with the task ID obtain from previous step, monitor the UBB FW task in progress untill it reaches 100 percent.
6. Perform an AC cycle, see AC Power Cycle System Sequence Check

"\1. Execute the following command:

'{""DateTime"":""<DATE_TIME>+00:00""}'
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to set the SMC Date and Time.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

【During Test】
1.Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to list all systemlog services collection.
Example:
curl -k -X GET http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices
2. Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET 'http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries'
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to query all SMC Event logs.
Example:
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries' >> event.log
3. Each dump of an event log is a maximum of 1000 entries using the Redfish command. Based on
the count from the previous example, there are 5762 events. To retrieve all the entries in the event
log, use the following command for the next page and repeat until ""$skip=5000"" for all events is
reached.
Example: To get page 2 - page 6 of redfish event.
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries?$skip=1000' >> event.log
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries?$skip=2000' >> event.log
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries?$skip=3000' >> event.log
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries?$skip=4000' >> event.log
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries?$skip=5000' >> event.log
4. Based on the Step 2 and 3 generated event log, query for “CPER” event. The CPER event will have
“AdditionalDataURI” that contains the cper.log to be retrieved for debug.
5.Execute the following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET 'http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --
output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
Description: Using BMC SSH, use the Redfish command to query all the SMC Event logs
Example:
curl -k -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/78535/attachment’ –-output /
tmp/5608.cper
6. Transfer the CPER file to Host/SUT and execute the following command to decode the downloaded
CPER file.
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json
Example:
cdump_analyzer -i 5608.cper -o 5608.cper.json

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1. Use the OOB Method to change the Power Limit Watts.
a. Remote into the BMC to retrieve and set the value for Power Limit Watts and check the value
using ROCm tools.
b. Through BMC SSH, use Redfish command to retrieve the current reading for Power Limit
Watts, the “SetPoint” value will indicate the current Max Power Limit Watts. Execute the
following command:
~ # curl -k -X GET http://<VNIC_IP>/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM/EnvironmentMetrics
By executing the command below, it will cycle through and list out for all OAMs
EnvironmentMetrics.
Example:
~ # for OAM in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do curl -k -X GET http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM/EnvironmentMetrics ; done
c. Through BMC SSH, use Redfish command to set value for Power Limit Watts, the “SetPoint”
value will modify the value stated. Execute the following command:
~ # for OAM in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do curl -k -X PATCH -d '{""PowerLimitWatts"": {""SetPoint"": <value>}}'
http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM/EnvironmentMetrics ; done
Executing this command below will cycle through and change to the preferred value for all
OAM “PowerLimitWatts.SetPoint”.
Example:
~ # for OAM in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do curl -k -X PATCH -d '{""PowerLimitWatts"": {""SetPoint"": 550}}' http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM/EnvironmentMetrics ; done
d. After setting the value for Power Limit Watts, verify the value changes by repeating step b
above.
e. Through SUT SSH, use ROCm tool to check the Power Limit Watts, the max power capping is shown as MAX_POWER from the output, and the current value of power capping is SOCKET_POWER. Execute the following command.
$ sudo amd-smi static  --limit | grep POWER

2. Use the In-Band Method to change the Power Limit Watts.
a. Through SUT SSH, use the command to list down and check current Power Limit Watts.
Execute the following command:
$ amd-smi static --limit
b. Through SUT SSH, use the following command to set the Power Limit Watts to any value.
$ sudo amd-smi set -g all --power-cap <value>
Example:
$ sudo amd-smi set -g all --power-cap 550
Through SUT SSH, use the following command to reset the Power Limit Watts back to original
value.
$ sudo amd-smi reset -g all --power-cap

3. Refer to Max Power Test to test out the max power capping function with workload

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
PASS:

method.

Capping value.

items.risk: RISK: changing GPU power capping affects thermal/power behaviour of the OAM modules; do not auto-run, apply with careful intent and reset afterwards.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

【During Test】
1. Use amd-smi for further read out of temperature, power, and gfxclk frequency with the following command:
amd-smi monitor -w 5
2. Run the following command in a separate terminal:
./agt -i=0,5,10,15,20,25,30,35 -unilog=PM -unilogallgroups -unilogperiod=50 -clkrestore -unilogoutput=pm_xxx.csv
Description: AGT tool to collect unilog for all GPU. The log samples every 50ms indicated with -
unilog period. Below information will be available in the log located in AGT run directory.
Timestamp , All-related GPU infrastructure power readings, All-related GPU clock frequency, GPU
XGMIRead Write bandwidth, and more.
3. Start system logging. Poll, monitor and collect: Ambient Inlet Temperature, System Fan Speeds,
Power Supply Output Power. Collect these data via Redfish
4.Allow the system (GPUs and CPUs) to Idle for a minimum of one (1) minute to allow temperatures to stabilize at an idle workload nominal temperature, GPU GFXCLKs to dynamically decrease to lower states, System Fan speeds to enter low power states that reduce system fan speed and reduce power supply loads that lead to decreased power dissipation, and Power Supply loads to decrease. This period will allow us to synchronize data more easily between the individual GPU logs, system logs, and DGEMM output logs. If the fan speed does not decrease within this idle period, you may need to increase the idle time for this step accordingly and restart the test.
5. Coralgemm
Run the workload Coralgemm module for 40 minutes. Be sure to capture output logs showing
GFLOP performance per DGEMM run within the looped test.
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided &
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 ./gemm R_64F R_64F R_64F R_64F OP_N OP_T 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 8640 96 2400 strided
6. Allow the system (GPUs and CPUs) to Idle for a minimum of one (1) minute to allow the following:
– temperatures to decrease
– GPU GFXCLKs to dynamically transition to lower power states
– System Fan speeds to decrease
– Power Supply loads to decrease.
This idle wait period will effectively create a distinct log data signature to allow data synchronization more easily between the individual GPU logs, system logs, and DGEMM output logs, especially when they may have different sampling periods
7. Finalize the test. Stop all logging and collect all log files. Pull and scrub the system logs for any GPUreported errors. Graph the relevant data with a common X-axis so that events correlate across plots. The idle periods before and after the test will help align samples, especially where the system, GPU or workload logs have different sampling periods. Allow the full vertical range on the Y-axis for Power and fan speed. Focus the Y-axis range on the Y-axis for: GPU TGP, GPU Temp, GPU GFXCLK, DGEMM GFLOPs

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).  

【During Test】
1.  Execute the following command for injecting ODECC correctable error to device_id = 0, block_id = 0 (UMC) at address 0x800000000:
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 0 -s 2 -t 2 -a 0x800000000

OOB Check:
1. SSH into BMC Console and run the following command to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""""Id"""": """"[^""""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to check OOB event entries:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries'
3. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
4. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o """"<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper""""
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp -o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper """"<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/""""
5. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json

Inband Check:
1. Run the following command to dump inband cper from amdgpuras tool:
$ sudo amdgpuras -C

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
• PASS = 
- AMDGPURAS tool UMC error injection command returns successfully
- Redfish command for CPER index retrieval shows the CPER index is increased by 1 and new CPER file is generated upon the error injected.
- The decoded result from the decoded CPER log matches the injected error type and location.
• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: UMC.
• Errorcode ext is 0 and Errocode ext Type is HBMEccErr (On-die ECC).
• Error severity matches the type of error you injected: Corrected error.
- The inband CPER log matches the OAM devices and error severity level

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

【During Test】
Ensure that the USB management interface is connected to a USB root port on the host BMC.

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: The USB2.0 link between HMC and BMC enumerates to high speed through dmesg.
items.ai_commands:
-- US.1_USB2.0 Interface between HMC and BMC: verify the HMC-BMC USB2.0 link enumerates to high speed. Agent checks the USB tree for the HMC management port
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP"lsusb -t 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE 'usb 2-?[0-9]|SuperSpeed|high-speed usb' | tail -n 20 2>&1"
items.ai_logs_output: return the lsusb -t tree + the USB high-speed enumeration dmesg lines so the user confirms the HMC-BMC USB2.0 link enumerates at high speed.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

【During Test】
1. Perform 1000x AC power cycles.
2. Perform 1000x DC power cycles.
3. Perform 1000x warm reboot.

Ensure all PCIe devices seen on the host system are enumerated with the expected speed width through lspci.
The following are examples of PCIe devices to check:
1. GPU
2. ConnectX(CX7 or CX8)
3. BlueField (BF3 or BF4)
4. SSD
5. PCIe Swtiches
6. PCIe retimers

Ensure all NVIDIA NVSwitch devices are detected by Infiniband with the expected speed and width:
1. MST status -s

Check if the full power sequencing has been completed.

Check if all I2C end points are on the bus through the I2C scan.

Check if the USB path from HMC to system BMC is up.

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: There are no issues pertaining to PCIe, Infiniband/Ethernet, power sequencing, I2C, and USB check.
items.ai_commands: -- SY.1_Power cycling and reboot testing: 1000x AC + 1000x DC power cycles + 1000x reboots is a long physical power-cycle stress needing PDU/AC control (operator) + IPMI DC cycles; agent automates the DC cycle loop via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power cycle 2>&1" and checks PCIe/IB/I2C/USB after, but AC cycles are operator.
items.ai_logs_output: return per-DC-cycle status + post-check (PCIe/Infiniband/Ethernet/I2C/USB) so the user confirms no sequencing issues across the cycles; AC-cycle log from the PDU.
items.risk: RISK: thousands of power cycles is long-running and physically disruptive; dedicated SUT + operator PDU control + approval.

items.procedure: Test connections between BMC I2C-2 and HPM0
items.criteria: BMC can successfully communicate with I2C devices on first HPM
items.ai_commands: -- IC.1_BMC I2C-2, and 1P functional is a physical I2C-connection test; the agent can partially verify device reachability on BMC I2C bus I2C-2 via `i2cdetect -y I2C-2` / `i2cget` on the BMC console (confirm the expected BMC I2C devices respond), but the mechanical connection check + photos is operator-performed.

items.risk: RISK: probing I2C requires care not to disturb live connectors; do not force I2C operations that could write to EEPROM. Connection integrity is physical - final judgment by operator.

items.procedure:
Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT
Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool
Test procedure:
1. BIOS settings:
   a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled
   b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE
   c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5)
   d. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listgmilinks
6. Run IOD Correctable Error Injection
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 0 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 0
7. Run CCD Correctable Error Injection
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 1 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 0
items.criteria: 1.Check BMC event log display correct information for RAS
items.ai_packages_needed: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool + HDT (user provisioned)
items.ai_commands: -- requires the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (with HDT/RDIMM-ECC setup) to inject an ADDC error, then verify the BMC event/SEL log shows the correct RAS record. Agent needs the exact injection command + HDT environment from the user (special tool/hardware); after injection, query BMC SEL.
items.ai_logs_output: return the injection result + `ipmitool sel list` / BMC event-log filtered to the ADDC RAS entry so user confirms the log displays correct info.
items.risk: RISK: fault injection via a hardware error-injection tool can disturb the OS; run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact tool command from user

items.procedure:
Send in-band command in localhost:
Set BIOS Debug Data: Disable
ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x70 0x00   

Set BIOS Debug Data: Enable
ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x70 0x01  

Get BIOS Debug Data
iptmiool raw 0x3a 0x71

Send out-of-band command:
Set BIOS Debug Data: Disable
ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> -C 17 raw  0x3a 0x70 0x00 from a remote client.

Set BIOS Debug Data: Enable
ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> -C 17 raw  0x3a 0x70 0x01 from a remote client.

Get BIOS Debug Data
ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC IP> -U <BMC username> -P <BMC password> -C 17 raw  0x3a 0x71 from a remote client.
items.criteria:
1. Command should be sent without any error.
2. Parameters should be shown correctly.
items.ai_commands: -- set/get BIOS Debug Data is state-changing. IB: `ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x70 0x00` (disable) or `0x01` (enable), then `ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x70` to get; OOB: same via `-I lanplus -H $BMC_IP -U $BMC_USER -P $BMC_PASS -C 17`. Confirm the target state with the user, then read it back.
items.ai_logs_output: return the set + get raw bytes (must send without error) and the read-back parameter so user confirms it matches the state set.
items.risk: RISK: changes the BIOS debug-data enable state; confirm target state and restore after the check

3.curl -k -u root:0penBmc \

>   -d '{"HTTPBasicAuth": "Disabled"}' \
>   https://10.35.228.145/redfish/v1/AccountService
3.curl -k -u root:0penBmc https://10.35.228.145/redfish/v1/Systems -i
>>>>show "HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized"
4.ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x41-- factory reset

items.ai_commands:
-- Add HTTPBasicAuth - Redfish: verify the HTTPBasicAuth toggle on the BMC AccountService. Baseline GET (expect 200), PATCH HTTPBasicAuth=Disabled, re-GET (expect 401), then restore via factory reset. Disabling basic auth is state-changing and can lock out access - the operator approves before the agent runs it.
curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -i https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems 2>&1 | head -n 12
curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PATCH -d '{"HTTPBasicAuth":"Disabled"}' https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/AccountService 2>&1
curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -i https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systems 2>&1 | head -n 12
-- restore: `ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x41` (factory reset) re-enables basic auth (operator/system).
items.ai_logs_output: return the baseline GET response (expect 200), the PATCH response for HTTPBasicAuth=Disabled, the re-GET (expect 401), and the post factory-reset GET so the user confirms the auth toggle and restore.
items.risk: RISK: disabling basic auth can lock out management access; the factory reset restores it - operator approve before the state change.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check security mode could be change
1. Asserted TPM physical presence by on-board jumper or switch
2. Power on SUT and enter into F1 setup.
3. Navigate to Security page to enable secure boot and TPM function.
4. Change Security Boot mode to another mode .
5. Save and reboot system.
6. Check Secyrity mode has been changed.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: 1. Security mode can be changed successfully.
items.ai_commands: -- Security mode (sheet-B): change Secure Boot mode/TPM via the BIOS Security page. Agent can read the current secure-boot/TPM state from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mokutil --sb-state 2>&1; if [ -e /sys/class/tpm/tpm0 ]; then ls /sys/class/tpm/; fi 2>&1"; the mode change requires an operator to assert TPM physical presence (jumper/switch), enter F1 setup, enable Secure Boot+TPM, change the mode and reboot.
items.ai_logs_output: return the secure-boot state (mokutil --sb-state) + TPM device presence so the user confirms the current state before the operator changes the Security mode in BIOS.
items.risk: RISK: changing Secure Boot mode needs TPM physical-presence assertion (jumper/switch) and BIOS setup access - operator/setup page required; do not auto-run.

items.ai_commands:
-- TH.1_Thermal Stress Test: run a full-power thermal stress on the DUT (CPU/GPU + external components) and confirm no thermal warnings/faults are logged. The worst-case ambient / thermal chamber is operator setup.
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP"stress-ng --cpu 0 --cpu-method all --timeout ${THERMAL_DURATION:?operator sets the soak duration} 2>&1 | tail -n 15; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader 2>&1"
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'TEMP|THERMAL' | head -n 30
items.ai_logs_output: return the thermal stress run log + the OOB thermal sensor reads (ipmitool sensor get temp) so the user confirms no thermal warnings/faults were logged.

items.criteria:
When completed, the diagnostic will return 0 to the shell if completed
normally. If an error occurs, it will return 1 to the shell, and if a retest is
required it will return 2. It will also print “PASS”, “FAIL”, or “RETEST” to
the screen.
PASS – The hardware passes the diagnostics
FAIL – The hardware has failed the diagnostics
RETEST – The hardware setup has failed the pre-check portion of the
diagnostics and a warning message appears describing the problem.
Correct the problem per the pre-check message and then test again.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Bios Setting
 EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled
 EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled
 EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled
 EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’]
 EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled
 EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled
2. Deploy Intel ITP environment.
3. Boot SUT into Windows.
4. Execute Intel Cscripts on the client
5. Using the following command
 >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log")
 >>>halt()
 >>>pcie.topology()
 >>>pcie.port_map()
6. Check PCIe slot target
 >>>ei.injUpiDataLinkFailover(socket,port,1,0x3)
 >>>go

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. System should work normally
2. BMC error log may record upi link disable/degrade(advanced) or correctable error(standard)
3. Front Panel fault Light will not Light if CPU is standard RAS SKU
4. Front Panel fault Light will Light if CPU is advanced RAS SKU
5. uEFI SEL Log may record same event
items.ai_packages_needed: Intel error-injection Cscripts/harness (user/FAE provides) + EDKII unlock (person/BMC, BIOS setup)
items.ai_commands: -- Socket 0~N (Intel UPI data-lane failover on Socket 0~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'upi|datalane|failover|lane'; echo __UPI_data-lane_failover_on_Socket_0~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".
items.ai_logs_output: return the injection harness result + UPI data-lane failover on Socket 0~N dmesg/mce tail + BMC SEL, so the user confirms the right handler fired and the expected SEL/uEFI-log entry was recorded.
items.risk: RISK: fault-injection test; needs BIOS CScripts/EDKII unlock + a person to drive the injector; injection can crash the SUT. Run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact injection script confirmed by the user/FAE.

items.items: DIMM VR over temperature via heat gun
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Setup the system to a standard supported configuration.
2. Boot to OS.
3. Use a heat gun to slowly heat the DIMM VR indicated under Configurations to the TWarning Threshold (Monitor the temperature increase via BMC web interface)
4. Once TWarning Threshold is reached, slowly proceed to add heat until TCritical threshold is reached.   (NOTE:  If you go too fast you may only trip the TCritical Threshold)

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Sensor value should be OK in the reasonable range.
2. Sensor value is same as ipmi sdr command and web ui.
3. SEL should have an event log when sensor reach to threshold.
items.ai_packages_needed: heat gun (operator) + ipmitool; lm-sensors for OS sensor read
items.ai_commands: -- DIMM VR over temperature via heat gun: verify DIMM VR over-temperature protection by heating the DIMM VR with a heat gun (physical, operator-driven). Agent captures the resulting OS/BMC thermal evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | grep -iE 'thermal|temp|trip|over.temp|throttle'; echo __DIMM_VR_TEMP; ipmitool sdr elist 2>&1 | grep -iE 'temp' | tail -30 2>&1"
items.ai_logs_output: return the thermal dmesg (trip/throttle) + BMC temp SDR readouts so the user confirms the VR over-temp protection engaged and throttled the DIMM.
items.risk: RISK: applying heat to the DIMM VR must be done carefully by the operator to avoid damage; agent only reads the resulting thermal evidence.

sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 0 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 0
7. Run CCD Correctable Error Injection

items.test_set: AMD CPU RAS -DRAM Correctable Implicit Error (Persistent)
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT
Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool

1.1 DRAM settings:
    a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled
    b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: NoLeakMode
    c. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Start Count: FFFE (Deviate from default setting FFF5)
    d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto
    e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False
    f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled
    g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled

1.2 MCA settings:
    a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled
    b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: Disabled
    c. CPU Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Enable: True
    d. UMC Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5)
    d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto
    e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False
    f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled
    g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled

2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listvalidumc
6. Implicit correctable error injection, enter command:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --dramecc --errormode 0 --socketdieumc 0:0:3 --setinjectionmode 1 --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 0

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check SUT will take correct activity as PCIE correctable error via AMD RAS Tool

1. BIOS settings:
   a. NBIO Common options → ACS Enable: Enable
   b. NBIO Common options → Enable AER Cap: Enable
   c. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Root Port UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   d. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Device UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
   f.  NBIO Common Options → NBIO RAS Common Options → SyncFlood on PCIe Fatal Error: True
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Execute the following command to get a list of devices in the PCIe slots:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listpcieslotsbdfinfo
6. PCIe Correctable Error inject to end device, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjbiopcie --segment 0 --bus 65 --device 0 --function 0 --errortype 0
7. PCIe Correctable Error inject to root port, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjbiopcie --segment 0 --bus 64 --device 1 --function 1 --errortype 0

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
Noted: EINJ-based correctable error injection is completed by triggering PCIe LCRC error at root port or end device.
items.ai_packages_needed: AMD RAS fault-injection tool (amdgpuras, AmdMemoryErrorTool) - needs packages in place first
items.ai_commands: -- PCIe slot 1~N: inject an AMD CPU RAS correctable PCIe error via the AMD RAS tool (amdgpuras/AmdMemoryErrorTool), then verify the error is logged sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg | tail -n 40; rasdaemon -r 2>&1"; fault-injection is interactive.
items.ai_logs_output: return the dmesg error log + rasdaemon record so the user confirms the PCIe correctable error was captured and (for correctable) the slot/memory stayed functional.
items.risk: RISK: correctable fault injection stresses the memory controller/platform and may reset it; run per AMD guidance with packages installed first and discuss exact steps after setup.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check SUT will take correct activity as PCIE uncorrectable non-fatal error via AMD RAS Tool

1. BIOS settings:
   a. NBIO Common options → ACS Enable: Enable
   b. NBIO Common options → Enable AER Cap: Enable
   c. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Root Port UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   d. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Device UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
   f.  NBIO Common Options → NBIO RAS Common Options → SyncFlood on PCIe Fatal Error: True
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Execute the following command to get a list of devices in the PCIe slots:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listpcieslotsbdfinfo
6. PCIe Uncorrectable non-fatal Error inject to end device, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjbiopcie --segment 0 --bus 65 --device 0 --function 0 --errortype 6
7. PCIe Uncorrectable non-fatal Error inject to root port, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjbiopcie --segment 0 --bus 64 --device 1 --function 1 --errortype 6

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For Uncorrectable errors, the tool provides a PASS status.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
Noted: EINJ-based uncorrectable nonfatal error injection is completed by triggering PCIe Poisoned TLP error at root port or end device.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC Plug a NIC (Network Interface Card) device on a target PCIe slot on the SUT / HDT
Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool

1. BIOS settings:
   a. NBIO Common options → ACS Enable: Enable
   b. NBIO Common options → Enable AER Cap: Enable
   c. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Root Port UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   d. AMD PBS → RAS → Pcie Device UnCorr Error Sev Reg: 7EF6030
   e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
   f.  NBIO Common Options → NBIO RAS Common Options → SyncFlood on PCIe Fatal Error: True
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Execute the following command to get a list of devices in the PCIe slots:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listpcieslotinfo
6. PCIe LCRC TX Error, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --pcieerror --sockdienbio 0:0:1 --errortype 0 --pciecore 3 --pcieport 0
7. PCIe LCRC RX Error, enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --pcieerror --sockdienbio 0:0:1 --errortype 1 --pciecore 3 --pcieport 0

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
items.ai_packages_needed: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (interactive, must install) + HDT/serial-debug unlock + RAS-capable DIMM/hardware
items.ai_commands: -- PCIe slot 1~N: inject the PCIe LCRC on PCIe slot 1~N via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'pcier|aer|ecrc|lcrc|poisoned|fatal'; echo __PCIe_LCRC_on_PCIe_slot_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.
items.ai_logs_output: return the AMD RAS tool injection result + PCIe LCRC on PCIe slot 1~N dmesg tail/mce + BMC SEL, so the user confirms the correct handler fired and the system recovered per the AMD RAS spec.
items.risk: RISK: fault-injection test; requires HDT/serial unlock + specific BIOS knobs (set by a person/BMC) and the injected error can disrupt/crash the SUT. Run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact injection mode confirmed by the user/FAE; do not leave the injector/hardware in a faulted state after verifying.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT
Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool

1. BIOS settings:
   a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled
   b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE
   c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5)
   d. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --dferror --socket 0 --errortype 1
6. The system will reset immediately.
7. When system boot into operating system again, check dmesg log.
8. To ensure sync_flood was triggered correctly, use HDT to check that FCH::PM:: S5_RESET_STATUS[SyncFlood]=1

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.

    【During Test】
    Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT
Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool

1. BIOS settings:
   a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled
   b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE
   c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5)

   e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable
2. Unlock CPU via HDT.
3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022.
4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software.
5. Enter the following commands:
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listtwixwafllinks
6. WAFL Correctable error injection at Socket 1
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --twixwafl --linknumber "WAFL lnk num" --errorlocation 0  --errortype 0
7. WAFL Correctable error injection at Socket 0
sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --twixwafl --linknumber "WAFL lnk num" --errorlocation 1  --errortype 0

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status.
2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed.
3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
items.ai_packages_needed: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (interactive, must install) + HDT/serial-debug unlock + RAS-capable DIMM/hardware
items.ai_commands: -- WAFL Correctable Error: inject the WAFL WAFL Correctable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'wafl|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __WAFL_WAFL_Correctable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.
items.ai_logs_output: return the AMD RAS tool injection result + WAFL WAFL Correctable Error dmesg tail/mce + BMC SEL, so the user confirms the correct handler fired and the system recovered per the AMD RAS spec.
items.risk: RISK: fault-injection test; requires HDT/serial unlock + specific BIOS knobs (set by a person/BMC) and the injected error can disrupt/crash the SUT. Run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact injection mode confirmed by the user/FAE; do not leave the injector/hardware in a faulted state after verifying.

    setenv serverip <TFTP Server>​

3. After BMC reboot , check BMC function should work normally.

"
items.ai_packages_needed: BMC UART console + TFTP server + BMC image (operator)
items.ai_commands: -- Uboot flash: plug the BMC UART console and flash the BMC image through the uBoot TFTP/sf flow. The flash steps are done over the physical BMC UART console by an operator; the agent only stages the image and verifies the BMC responds afterwards OOB from the agent host: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'Firmware Revision' 2>&1
items.ai_logs_output: operator runs the uBoot tftp/sf update on the BMC UART, reboots the BMC and confirms it flashes successfully; agent verifies BMC responds + FW revision after.
items.risk: RISK: flashing the BMC via UART is destructive and can brick the BMC; operator-only with the approved image.
