items.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - Memory Demand and Patrol Scrub
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).
3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation
Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling
The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts:
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration >
	— EV DFX Features = Enable
	— Disable BIOS Done = [X]

ELOG Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Error Support= Enable
	— EMCA Logging Support= Enable
	— Corrected Error eLog = Enable
	— Memory Error eLog = Enable
	— Processor Error eLog = Enable

Error Reporting Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings >
	— WHEA Support = Enable
	— WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable

Error Injection Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log >
	— System Errors = Enable
	— System Memory Poison = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings >
	— MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling >
	— IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable
	— IIO MCA Support = Disable
	— IIO eDPC Support = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable

Firmware First Model
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Logging Support = Enable
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0
	— EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable

Crash Log
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable

4. Other OS Notes
You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable".

【During Test】
1. Patrol Scrub specific BIOS setup :
EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration >
	— Patrol Scrub = Enable at End of Post
	— Patrol Scrub Interval = 1
	— DDR5 ECS = Enable
EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration >
	— PTRR DDR Enable = Disable 

2. Ensure that patrol scrub is enabled on the DIMM that will be encountering the memory CECC error.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.scrubctl
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.scrubctl.showfields()

3. Ensure that the machine check status register and retry_rd_err_logs are clear.
Check that en_patspr is enabled in the corresponding DIMM location to log patrol
scrub errors.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow")
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[0].showfields()

4. Inject a correctable patrol scrub error.
>>> halt()
>>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck()
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(0x8000, errType="ce", PatrolConsume=True)

5. Review the machine check bank registers. Verify that a correctable patrol scrub
error was logged in the MSCOD.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow")
>>>
sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.showfields()

6. The retry_rd_err_log will also indicate a patrol scrub error was logged.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log.showfields()

7. Resume the system and check the serial log that BIOS handled the error.
>>> go()

【After Test】
1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Verify that an ELog record was generated indicated by extlog_mem_event.
items.ai_packages_needed: Intel error-injection Cscripts/harness (user/FAE provides) + EDKII unlock (person/BMC, BIOS setup)
items.ai_commands: -- Patrol Scrub (Intel memory Patrol Scrub error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'scrub|patrol|demand|corrected'; echo __memory_Patrol_Scrub; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".
items.ai_logs_output: return the injection harness result + memory Patrol Scrub dmesg/mce tail + BMC SEL, so the user confirms the right handler fired and the expected SEL/uEFI-log entry was recorded.
items.risk: RISK: fault-injection test; needs BIOS CScripts/EDKII unlock + a person to drive the injector; injection can crash the SUT. Run only on a dedicated SUT with the exact injection script confirmed by the user/FAE.

items.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - Full Memory Mirroring
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).
3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation
Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling
The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts:
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration >
	— EV DFX Features = Enable
	— Disable BIOS Done = [X]

ELOG Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Error Support= Enable
	— EMCA Logging Support= Enable
	— Corrected Error eLog = Enable
	— Memory Error eLog = Enable
	— Processor Error eLog = Enable

Error Reporting Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings >
	— WHEA Support = Enable
	— WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable

Error Injection Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log >
	— System Errors = Enable
	— System Memory Poison = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings >
	— MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling >
	— IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable
	— IIO MCA Support = Disable
	— IIO eDPC Support = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable

Firmware First Model
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Logging Support = Enable
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0
	— EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable

Crash Log
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable

4. Other OS Notes
You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable".

【During Test】
1. UCE on Primary Channel specific BIOS setup :
• Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration >
	— Mirror Mode = Full Mirror Mode
• Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration >
	— Enforce Population POR = Disable
• Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population.

2. Complete steps 1-6 in the CE recipe to check on the state of the system, find an address to inject to, and to unlock the injectors.

3. Choose the target device for error injection and modify masks for a multi-device uncorrectable ECC error injection.
>>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=2, dev1msk=0x3)

4. Inject and consume the uncorrectable ECC error.
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="uce", verbose=True)

5. Check the B2CMI MC bank to verify that the injection was successful. For easier decoding, read the B2CMI shadow registers. For MCi_STATUS check that all the
bit-fields are the same as shown next. MCi_ADDR should align with the injection address in the previous step. For MCi_MISC, the bit-fields of interest which should be logged as shown next are: mirrorcorrerr (mirror corrected the error and mirror scrub was successful), mccmdmirrregion (transaction was to a mirrored region), and bankindex (value should align with the memory controller of the injection target).
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_addr_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow.show()
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow.show()

6. Resume the system to allow all error handling flows to complete.
>>> go()

items.items: UCE on Primary, CE on Secondary
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).
3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation
Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling
The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts:
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration >
	— EV DFX Features = Enable
	— Disable BIOS Done = [X]

ELOG Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Error Support= Enable
	— EMCA Logging Support= Enable
	— Corrected Error eLog = Enable
	— Memory Error eLog = Enable
	— Processor Error eLog = Enable

Error Reporting Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings >
	— WHEA Support = Enable
	— WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable

Error Injection Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log >
	— System Errors = Enable
	— System Memory Poison = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings >
	— MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling >
	— IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable
	— IIO MCA Support = Disable
	— IIO eDPC Support = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable

Firmware First Model
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Logging Support = Enable
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0
	— EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable

Crash Log
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable

4. Other OS Notes
You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable".

【During Test】
1. UCE on Primary, CE on Secondary specific BIOS setup :
• Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration >
	— Mirror Mode = Full Mirror Mode
• Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration >
	— Enforce Population POR = Disable
• Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population.

2. Complete steps 1-6 in the CE recipe to check on the state of the system, find an address to inject to, and to unlock the injectors. 

3. Using the desired target address, arm the injectors on the secondary channel for acorrectable ECC error and do not inject or consume.
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="ce", immInject=False, immConsume=False, Inj2ndCh=True, verbose=True, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False)

4. Using the desired target address, arm the injectors on the primary channel for an uncorrectable ECC error and do not inject or consume. The order of this step and the previous step does not matter.
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="uce", immInject=False, immConsume=False, Inj2ndCh=False, verbose=True, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False)

5. Check the state of the memory error injectors to verify that they are armed as expected. For this particular target address, the primary channel is {socket 0, mc 0, channel 0 (only 1 channel per IMC so redundant)} and it's shown that the injector is armed for a multi-device ECC error which is uncorrectable. Also shown is the injector on the secondary channel (mc 1) which is armed for a single device single bit ECC error which is correctable.
>>> ei.mem.showMemInjectors(socket=0)

6. Write to the target address. 0xcafecafecafecafe was chosen as an example.
>>> itp.threads[0].mem("0x000100000000p", 8, 0xcafecafecafecafe)

7. Write back invalidate all the caches so modified cachelines will be written back toDDR5 memory. This action will inject the errors to memory.
>>> itp.threads[0].wbinvd()

8. Check that the memory error injectors are now unarmed since the write back invalidate injected the errors.
>>> ei.mem.showMemInjectors(socket=0)

9. Read the target address to consume the errors. The primary data will be read first, an uncorrectable ECC error will be detected, secondary (mirrored) data will be
read, a correctable ECC error will be detected, corrected, logged, mirror scrub and check on the primary channel will occur, and the good data will be delivered to the requester.
>>> itp.threads[0].mem('0x000100000000p', 8)

10. Check the primary channel's B2CMI MCA bank. There should be a valid (valid==1) corrected (uc==0) MCA error indicating a read ECC error (mscod==1) with a
corrected error count (corrcount) of 1.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow.showfields()\n

11. Primary B2CMI's MCi_ADDR should match the target address.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_addr_shadow

12. Primary B2CMI's MCi_MISC should indicate that the following: error was corrected during mirroring and mirror scrub was successful (mirrorcorrerr==1), transaction was to a mirrored region (mccmdmirrregion==1), mccmdvld==1 to indicate the other mccmd fields are valid, mirror scrub check read returned good data (errortype[3]==1), and the transaction couldn't be corrected by ECC (errortype[2]==1).
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow.showfields()\n

13. The secondary channel's IMC should have a valid (valid==1) corrected (UC==0) MCA error indicating that there was a corrected demand read ECC error (mscod==0x80) with a corrected error count (corrcount) of 1.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.showfields()\n

14. Secondary IMC's MCi_ADDR should match the target address.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc8_addr_shadow

15. Secondary IMC's MCi_MISC contains FRU identification details which are also logged in the retry read error logs. See the processor register specification for the decoding of IMC MCi_MISC.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_misc_shadow

16. Secondary IMC's retry read error logs configured to log demand read ECC errors should have valid data. Not going into fine detail here about what to expect
because there's another recipe that goes into detail about what to expect in the case of a corrected ECC error and the register definitions should be clear.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1].showfields()\n

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1].showfields()\n

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1].showfields()\n

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address3[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_parity[1]

17. Resume the system to allow all error handling flows to complete.
>>> go()

>>> error.check_mem_errors()

SDDC coverage differs depending on x4 or x8 DRAM based DIMMs so be aware of the DRAM topology of the installed DIMMs. Also, some enabled features impact the best possible ECC mode that the memory can operate in. For this test, directory mode was disabled and any other feature that may require metadata bits is not enabled. Therefore, the DDR memory is operating in 128b ECC mode.
>>> ras.mem.show_ecc_mode()

4. Check if the injectors are locked for all sockets and unlock if locked.

6. Inject and consume the correctable ECC error.

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc8_addr_shadow

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.show()

Based on this output, sets one and three will log demand/ufill read errors.

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address3[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_misc[1]
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_parity[1]

10. retry_rd_err_log. The ECC mode is 128b so PFD results for any single device errors are not interesting or useful because there is 100% detection and correction of single device errors. The most interesting bit-fields that should match are shown next. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1].show()

11. retry_rd_err_log_address1/2/3. These registers log the error location and address. All details should match with the error injection location specified and the IMC MC bank logs.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1].show()
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1].show()
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address3[1].show()

12. retry_rd_err_log_parity. Matches the mask specified in memDevs.
>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_parity[1].show()

13. Based on the logical rank that was injected to, check that the rank's corrected ECC error counter incremented by 1. For DDR5, the logical rank/chip-select is encoded as: {DIMM, rank. sub-channel}. There is a counter and threshold register for each of the eight possible ranks on the channel.

>>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.correrrthrshld

items.items: Out Of Band: UMC Uncorrectable Address Or Command Parity Single Shot
items.procedure:
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2.  Execute the following command to inject uncorrectable address/command parity error with single shot method to device_id = 0, block_id = 0 (UMC):
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 0 -s 4 -t 4 -m 1
3. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
4. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
5. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o ""<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper""
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp –o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper ""<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/""
6. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json

• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: UMC.
• Errorcode ext is 4 and Errocode ext Type is AddressCommandParityErr.

items.procedure:
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2. Execute the following command for injecting uncorrectable address/command parity error with
persistent method to device_id = 0, block_id = 0 (UMC):
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 0 -s 4 -t 4 -m 2
3. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1

# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
5. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.

password for the prompt.
$ scp –o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper ""<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/""

items.items: AMD GPU RAS tool version check
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).
    3. Download and install the latest AMD GPU RAS Tool on OS.
    ex. Ubuntu 22.04
    $ sudo dpkg -i amdgpuras*.deb

    【During Test】
    1. used commmand :sudo amdgpuras -v

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Tool version should be equal to or newer than 1.6.3
items.ai_commands: -- AMD GPU RAS tool version (min 1.6.3): sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "amdgpuras --version 2>&1"
items.ai_logs_output: return `amdgpuras --version`; confirm tool version >= the required minimum (1.6.3). No RISK (read-only).

items.items: Out of Band: UMC Correctable ODECC
items.procedure:
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '"Id": "[^"]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2.  Execute the following command for injecting ODECC correctable error to device_id = 0, block_id = 0 (UMC) at address 0x800:
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 0 -s 2 -t 2 -a 0x800
3. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '"Id": "[^"]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
4. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
5. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o "<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper"
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp -o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper "<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/"
6. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json
items.criteria:
• PASS = 
- AMDGPURAS tool UMC error injection command returns successfully
- Redfish command for CPER index retrieval shows the CPER index is increased by 1 and new CPER file is generated upon the error injected.
- The decoded result from the decoded CPER log matches the injected error type and location.
• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: UMC.
• Errorcode ext is 0 and Errocode ext Type is HBMEccErr (On-die ECC).
• Error severity matches the type of error you injected: Corrected error.

items.ai_commands: -- In-band error injection (GFX Correctable Error Injection) via the amdgpuras tool: this targets a real GPU hardware error path and needs the exact amdgpuras invocation the user/FAE supplies for this unit+type. Agent then confirms injection succeeded and checks dmesg for the expected amdgpu hardware error.
items.ai_logs_output: return amdgpuras injection result (should show "Error inject successfully") + `dmesg -T | tail -100` showing the expected amdgpu hardware error, so user can confirm the injected error was handled per spec.
items.risk: RISK: hardware error injection can cause GPU errors/ECCs and may need a reboot; run only on a dedicated SUT and confirm the exact injection command/target with the user/FAE.

items.procedure:
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2.  Execute the following command to list down all supported XGMI links:
$ sudo amdgpuras -b 7 -l
3. Execute the following command to inject correctable error to xgmi_link = 1, block_id = 7 (XGMI):
$ sudo amdgpuras -b 7 -m 6 -t 2 -s 1
4. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
5. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper
6. Use scp command to copy downloaded CPER file from BMC to host. There are two ways to do the
transfer, either scp at host or scp at BMC console.
scp at host requires BMC details to fill in below (bmc_ip, bmc_user) and enter BMC login password
for the prompt.
$ scp -o ""<bmc_user>@<bmc_ip>:/tmp/<cper_index>.cper""
scp at BMC console, requires Host details to fill in below (host_ip, host_user) and enter Host login
password for the prompt.
$ scp -o /tmp/<cper_index>.cper ""<host_user>@<host_ip>:/home/<host_user>/""
7. Execute the following command to decode the downloaded CPER file:
$ cdump_analyzer -i <cper_index>.cper -o <cper_index>.cper.json
items.criteria:
• PASS = 
- AMDGPURAS tool XGMI error injection command returns successfully
- Redfish command for CPER index retrieval shows the CPER index is increased by 1 and new CPER file is generated upon the error injected.
- The decoded result from the decoded CPER log matches the injected error type and location.
• Error location lists the OAM on which the error occurred.
• Bank matches the type of error injected: XGMI.
• Errorcode ext is 6 and Errocode ext Type is BERExceededErr.
• Error severity matches the type of error injected: Corrected error.
items.ai_packages_needed: AMDGPU-RAS tool (OOB mode) + BMC Redfish access
items.ai_commands: -- Out-of-band XGMI Correctable error injection requires the amdgpuras OOB (BMC/Redfish) path + a Redfish query for the CPER index afterwards. Agent must confirm the exact OOB injection command with the user (board/component + target), then run injection and Redfish CPER check.
items.ai_logs_output: return amdgpuras injection result (should return success) + the Redfish CPER/index readout (via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -k -u bmc_user:bmc_pass https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Systemsystem/LogServices/CPER/Entries 2>&1" ) so user confirms a CPER entry was recorded.
items.risk: RISK: injecting an uncorrectable/hardware error can disrupt active GPUs / require recovery; run only on a dedicated SUT and confirm the exact injection target with the user/FAE.

    Benchmarking the CPU using SPEC CPU in Ubuntu 20.04 involves several steps. Here's a step-by-step guide to help you through the process:
Step:
1: Obtain SPEC CPU Benchmark Suite
Visit the SPEC website (https://www.spec.org/cpu/) and obtain the SPEC CPU benchmark suite. You will need to agree to the licensing terms and conditions before downloading the benchmark suite.

2: Install Dependencies
Before installing SPEC CPU, make sure your system has the necessary dependencies. You may need to install development tools, compilers, and other required libraries. On Ubuntu,you can do this by running:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential
3: Extract the Benchmark Suite
tar -xf <path_to_spec_archive>
4: Set Environment Variables
source shrc
5: Choose Benchmark Types
Within the SPEC CPU benchmark suite, there are multiple benchmark tests available. You can choose the benchmark types that align with your specific needs. You can run SPECint for integer-intensive workloads or SPECfp for floating-point-intensive workloads, or both.

6: Build the Benchmarks
./buildspec --config=linux64 --tune=base int
7: Run the Benchmarks
bash
Copy code
./runspectest --config=linux64 --tune=base --iterations=3 int
Replace int with fp if you are running SPECfp benchmarks.
8: Monitor and Record Results
During the benchmarking process, monitor system performance metrics, such as CPU utilization and memory usage. The results will be generated and stored in the appropriate benchmark directories.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    HPL is a free and portable implementation of the High-Performance Linpack Benchmark. 
It solves a random, dense system of linear equations using double-precision (64-bit) floating point arithmetic
and can be run on anything from credit card-sized computers to the world’s fastest supercomputers.
AMD provides a script that will download, build and install all HPL prerequisites.

Requirements:
AMD HPL is distributed in a tarball named hpl.tar.bz2. It requires Ubuntu 20.04 LTS or newer
and assumes that Ubuntu has been freshly installed. The installation script requires internet access to
download the necessary Ubuntu packages and source code. The installation script must be run as
root. HPL must also be run as root.

Test Procedure: 
Install HPL
1. The AMD HPL installation package is delivered as hpl.tar.bz2. Copy this archive into the
destination folder on the SuT and extract it as follows:
$ tar -xvf hpl.tar.bz2
2. After all of the files are extracted, run the installation script with root user/sudo privileges:
$ ./hpl-install-u2004-gcc9-v1.0.4.sh
3. This installation package will work on Ubuntu 20.04. HPL is a complex package and will take several
minutes to fully install.
4. After installation completes, enter the work directory:
$ cd hpl/work

Running HPL
1. Log into the SuT as the root user and navigate to the hpl/work directory. The HPL binary is named
xhpl, but it is not directly executed by the user. Instead, AMD has created a set of run files that are
automatically configured for your SuT by the AMD script generate_hpl_files_v1.0.4.py. To launch
HPL, execute:
$ ./run_hpl_ccx.sh
2. As the script name implies, HPL is run with one xhpl instance per CCX using eight OpenMP threads
per instance. Only physical cores are used regardless if SMT is enabled or not. In general, disabling
SMT will free up power to allow the physical cores to run at slightly higher clock speeds.
If your SuT configuration changes after HPL installation, execute generate_hpl_files_v1.0.4.py to
regenerate the appropriate run files. If you do not do this, results will be suboptimal or HPL will
crash. The generate_hpl_files_v1.0.4.py script will automatically detect system configuration
information and write the required HPL.dat and appfile_ccx files for you, which saves you the error
prone steps of doing this manually. To use generate_hpl_files_v1.0.4.py, execute the script as follows:
$ ./generate_hpl_files_v1.0.4.py
3. And then launch HPL:
$ ./run_hpl_ccx.sh

Note1: AMD does not recommend manually editing the HPL run files.
Note2: every AMD CPUs have different setting

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: the result should match with Intel/AMD spec
items.ai_packages_needed: AMD HPL (hpl.tar.bz2 - AMD-provided) + internet at install + build toolchain gcc/gfortran/BLAS
items.ai_commands: -- Linpack(HPL): run the AMD HPL Linpack benchmark. The AMD HPL tarball (hpl.tar.bz2) install script builds all prerequisites and needs internet + a freshly installed Ubuntu 20.04+; after the AMD HPL package is installed, the agent runs the benchmark and collects Gflops.
items.ai_logs_output: return the HPL run output (problem size, N,NB,P,Q,time, Gflops) so the user compares the achieved Gflops against the Intel/AMD spec.
items.risk: RISK: HPL runs at high CPU load for a long time; ensure adequate cooling and run in a maintenance window.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Measure memory performance by stream
Step:
1. download source code from Virginia University https://www.cs.virginia.edu/stream/FTP/Code/
2. compile source code via command "gcc -fopenmp -mcmodel=large -DSTREAM_TYPE=double -DSTREAM_ARRAY_SIZE=430080000 -DNTIMES=100 stream.c -o stream"
3. run benchmark "./stream"
4. The results will be displayed in the terminal window.
Here is an example of the output of the memory benchmark:
Function    Best Rate MB/s  Avg time     Min time     Max time
Copy:           17865.3     0.385696     0.385175     0.389823
Scale:          18366.1     0.375457     0.374672     0.377162
Add:            21355.5     0.492175     0.483337     0.493110
Triad:          21027.9     0.492038     0.490869     0.495802
-------------------------------------------------------------
Solution Validates: avg error less than 1.000000e-13 on all three arrays

Criteria:
The result must match the DIMM SPEC

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: The result must match the DIMM SPEC
items.ai_commands: -- Stream: run the STREAM memory-bandwidth benchmark on the DIMMs; needs stream compiled (gcc). Agent builds/runs stream.c and returns the bandwidth result; judge against DIMM spec by user.
items.ai_logs_output: return the FULL STREAM Triad/Copy/Add/Scale output (MB/s per core) so user confirms it matches the DIMM SPEC.
items.risk: RISK: STREAM is a short bench; ensure the SUT is otherwise idle for a stable number.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Fio Storage Performance

Step:
1.sudo apt install fio
2.vim seqread.fio
3.fill the content by test require that shows below

[global]
thread
ioengine=libaio
direct=1
group_reporting
norandommap=1
randrepeat=0
refill_buffers
clocksource=clock_gettime
overwrite=1
ramp_time=10s
runtime=43200s
time_based
threads=1
threads-per-queue=1
iodepth=1
rw=read
bs=512b
numjobs=1

4.save file
5.run command "./fio seqread.fio"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: fio will show performance result, it must match the spec.
items.ai_commands: -- FIO sequential read (100% read, QD1, bs=512B, numjobs=1) on a user-designated test volume: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "command -v fio >/dev/null 2>&1 || { apt-get update && apt-get install -y fio; }; FIO_TARGET=${FIO_TARGET:?set to a user-designated empty test volume}; RUNTIME=${RUNTIME:-60}; fio --name=seqread --filename=$FIO_TARGET --ioengine=libaio --direct=1 --units_base=1024 --rw=read --bs=512b --iodepth=1 --numjobs=1 --ramp_time=10s --runtime=$RUNTIME --time_based --group_reporting 2>&1 | grep -E "read:|IOPS|bw=" | tail -10"
items.ai_logs_output: return the full fio job output (read/write IOPS, BW MB/s, latency) from /tmp/seqread.log so the user diffs against the SSD performance spec. Sustained run (runtime set by user; item says 43200s) - confirm duration/approval.
items.risk: RISK: fio write/mix runs sustained destructive I/O on the drive; run only against a user-designated test volume and confirm the runtime first.

【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Prerequisites
Install Relevant Tools: Ensure that InfiniBand drivers and performance testing tools are installed (e.g., OFED).
Configure IPoIB (IP-over-InfiniBand):
Ensure the InfiniBand HCA is up and properly configured. You can check and configure using tools like ifconfig or ip.
Make sure ping works between the two machines over the InfiniBand network.
Environment Setup
Load Drivers: Ensure that the required kernel modules are loaded, such as ib_ipoib, ib_uverbs, and rdma_ucm.

modprobe ib_ipoib
modprobe ib_uverbs
modprobe rdma_ucm
Setup Hostname or IP: Ensure that the InfiniBand network on both testing machines is configured with IP addresses or hostnames.

Performance Testing
Latency Test
Use ibv_rc_pingpong for latency testing:

Run on Server Side:

ibv_rc_pingpong
Run on Client Side:

ibv_rc_pingpong <server_ip_or_hostname>
Bandwidth Test
Use ib_write_bw for bandwidth testing:

Run on Server Side:

ib_write_bw
Run on Client Side:

ib_write_bw <server_ip_or_hostname>
Detailed Steps
Prepare Server:

ibv_rc_pingpong
Run on Client:

ibv_rc_pingpong <server IP address or hostname>
Considerations
Multiple Tests: To get more accurate data, it is advisable to run the tests multiple times and take the average.
Different Test Modes: Depending on your requirements, you can try different modes such as RC (Reliable Connection), UC (Unreliable Connection), UD (Unreliable Datagram), etc.
Network Configuration: Ensure optimal network configuration, including MTU size, flow control settings, etc.
Concluding the Test
After the tests are completed, you can check the interface status and results using:

ifconfig
or

ip link show

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.procedure:
1.Install OFED driver
2.Set NIC ip (ex:ifconfig NIC1 10.10.10.1,NIC2 10.10.10.2)
3.Check NIC DUID via ibstat command.
4.Check NIC RDMA via mst status -v 
5.Set OpenSM ,if run NIC1&NIC2,
opensm -g (NIC1 GUID) && opensm -g (NIC2 GUID)
6.Run test command :taskset -c 30 ib_write_bw -d NIC1 RDMA  -i 1 -q 2 -p 11000 -D 3 --run_infinitely -F --report_gbits & sleep 3 ; ib_write_bw -d NIC2 RDMA -i 1 -q 2 -D 3 --run_infinitely -p 11000 10.10.10.1(NIC1 IP) -F --report_gbits
items.criteria:
1. Network bandwidth should match with SPEC definition during stress(98%).
2. System should be workable and no error message in system event log after stress.
3. Please save Procedure step 6 test log.
items.ai_packages_needed: Mellanox OFED (driver) + opensm + iperf/ib_write_bw + a peer IB host
items.ai_commands: -- ib_write_bw: install OFED, set NIC IPs, check DUID via `ibstat`, RDMA via `mst status -v`, start OpenSM, then sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ib_write_bw -d mlx5_0 --report_gbits 2>&1" against a peer; needs a reachable IB peer + OFED installed.
items.ai_logs_output: return ib_write_bw throughput result so the user confirms bandwidth >= 98% of spec during stress and the system stays workable.
items.risk: RISK: 98% bandwi width IB stress saturates the link; dedicated peer + approval.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】 

1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 

2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

  

【During Test】 

1. Password setting for 2 systems  

$ vim /etc/hosts  

OS IP SUT1 

OS IP SUT2 

2. Password-free Login 

$ ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 

$ ssh-copy-id root@SUT2 

$ ssh root@SUT2 

3. Install dependencies 

 $ sudo apt-get install libpmix-dev libfabric-dev libev-dev zlib1g-dev 

4. Download and uncompress the latest release of OpenMPI (5.0.5 at the time of this writing) 

$ wget https://download.open-mpi.org/release/open-mpi/v5.0/openmpi-5.0.5.tar.gz 

$ tar xzf openmpi-5.0.5.tar.gz 

$ cd openmpi-5.0.5/ 

  

【After Test】 

1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 

2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test
items.criteria:
1. The NCCL Multi node shoule be executed without errors. 

2. The result of NCCL should meet the spec of nvidia-performance benchmark document without errors.
items.ai_commands: -- Multi - Node - NCCL: run multi-node NCCL. Agent does the setup (hosts, password-free ssh, OpenMPI deps) then the NCCL allreduce on 2 nodes sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "apt-get install -y libpmix-dev libfabric-dev libev-dev zlib1g-dev 2>&1 | tail -n 3; mpirun --hostfile /etc/hosts -np 2 /path/nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 128M -f 2 2>&1 | tail -n 15 2>&1"; requires 2 SUT nodes + NCCL-tests + OpenMPI.
items.ai_logs_output: return the mpirun all_reduce_perf output (busbw/algBW per size) so the user confirms the multi-node NCCL runs without error and meets the NVIDIA performance doc spec.
items.risk: RISK: multi-node NCCL needs 2 hosts in the cluster with password-free SSH + full GPU bandwidth; not a one-liner, requires the cluster set up first.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】 

1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 

2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 

  

【During Test】 

1. Password setting for 2 systems  

$ vim /etc/hosts  

OS IP SUT1 

OS IP SUT2 

2. Password-free Login 

$ ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 

$ ssh-copy-id root@SUT2 

$ ssh root@SUT2 

3. Install dependencies 

 $ sudo apt-get install libpmix-dev libfabric-dev libev-dev zlib1g-dev 

4. Download and uncompress the latest release of OpenMPI (5.0.5 at the time of this writing) 

$ wget https://download.open-mpi.org/release/open-mpi/v5.0/openmpi-5.0.5.tar.gz 

$ tar xzf openmpi-5.0.5.tar.gz 

$ cd openmpi-5.0.5/ 

  
【After Test】 

1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 

2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. The NCCL Multi node shoule be executed without errors. 

2. The result of NCCL should meet the spec of nvidia-performance benchmark document without errors.
items.ai_commands: -- Multi-Node NCCL: set password-free SSH between the two SUTs, install OpenMPI deps, then run the NVIDIA multi-node NCCL benchmark and compare to spec. ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -N "" -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa 2>&1; ssh-copy-id root@${SUT2_IP:?multi-node peer IP} 2>&1; apt-get install -y libpmix-dev libfabric-dev libev-dev zlib1g-dev 2>&1
items.ai_logs_output: return the mpirun all_reduce_perf output (busbw/algBW per size) so the user confirms the multi-node NCCL runs without error and meets the NVIDIA performance doc spec.
items.risk: RISK: multi-node NCCL needs 2 hosts in the cluster with password-free SSH + full GPU bandwidth; not a one-liner, requires the cluster set up first.

items.items: FIO Mix read/write bandwidth/IOPS (70/30% read/write @ QD1, bs=512B, numjobs=1)
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Fio Storage Performance

Step:
1.sudo apt install fio
2.vim randwrite.fio
3.fill the content by test require that shows below

[global]
thread
ioengine=libaio
direct=1
group_reporting
norandommap=1
randrepeat=0
refill_buffers
clocksource=clock_gettime
overwrite=1
ramp_time=10s
runtime=43200s
time_based
threads=1
threads-per-queue=1
iodepth=1
rw=randwrite
bs=512b
numjobs=1

4.save file
5.run command "./fio randwrite.fio"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: fio will show performance result, it must match the spec.
items.ai_packages_needed: fio (install) + a user-designated EMPTY test volume (NOT the OS disk; fio overwrites it)
items.ai_commands:
-- FIO mix 70/30 read/write @ QD1 bs=512B numjobs=1 (DESTRUCTIVE, empty test volume only):
# fio mixed random read/write benchmark (DESTRUCTIVE I/O)
# FIO_TARGET must be a USER-DESIGNATED, EMPTY/clearable TEST VOLUME
items.ai_logs_output: return /tmp/fio-mix.log (read IOPS, write IOPS, BW MB/s, latency) and confirm the result matches the SSD spec. Destructive sustained I/O on the designated target only - confirm runtime first.
items.risk: RISK: fio randrw/randwrite performs sustained destructive overwrite; run ONLY against a user-designated empty test volume and confirm the runtime first. NEVER target the OS system disk (/, /boot) or any in-use volume.

items.criteria:

items.ai_commands: -- Power on with two sockets: CPU listing in BIOS Setup is human/KVM; agent reads the OS view with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "cat /proc/cpuinfo 2>&1 | grep -cE "^processor"; echo ---; dmidecode -t processor 2>&1 | grep -cE "Socket Designation"; echo ---; lscpu 2>&1 | grep -E "^CPU\(s\)|^Socket" 2>&1" to confirm two physical sockets are present and enumerated.

5. Power on the system and press boot up the Linux system.

8. Check the file “type7.txt”, get the following information and compare it with the given specification:
a. L1 Installed Size
b. L1 Maximum Size
c. L2 Installed Size
d. L2 Maximum Size
e. L3 Installed Size
f. L3 Maximim Size

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    IOmeter is a storage stress tool. For this test, it is used to test the PCIe and nvme communication busses.

1. Configure each drive as its own volume.
2. Boot to OS
3. Install IOmeter software.
4. Bring all HDD/SSD/NVME drives online and format
5. Run IOmeter.
6. Select the system in the “Topology” box to the left.
7. Under the “Disk Targets” Tab,
a. Select all volumes in the “Targets” box.
b. Set “# of Outstanding I/Os” to 16.
8. Under the “Access Specifications” Tab
a. Select “Default” in the box to the right, and click “Add”
9. Under the “Results Display” Tab
a. In the “Results Since” box click “Start of Test” to monitor the test progress
10. Click the Green Flag to begin the tests
11. IOmeter writes a test file to each volume if it is not already present. For larger storage footprints,
this can take several hours to complete. While IOmeter is doing this, it will display “Preparing
Drives” in an info bar.
12. After this, it will display bar graphs depicting the current results
13. The test should run for a minimum of 48 hours with no reported errors.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria: Pass: Test should run with no reported errors, system hangs, or reboots

Linux:

3. Check if the HDD/SSD drive just installed can be detected in the system:

    【After Test】

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    I. Build RAID:
1. Check disks: lsblk
2. Use mdadm to create software RAID: mdadm --create --auto=yes /dev/md3 --level=[0|1|5] --raid-devices=4 /dev/nvme2n1 /dev/nvme3n1 /dev/nvme4n1 /dev/nvme5n1 --run
3. Check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　Check that all disks should show “active sync”.

II. Setup RAID:
4. Format RAID: mkfs.ext4 -F /dev/md3
5. Check disks: lsblk
6. Create Folder: mkdir /mnt/raid
7. Mount RAID: mount /dev/md3 /mnt/raid
8. Check disks: lsblk

III. Transfer File:
9. Create a file: dd if=/dev/zero of=/root/512M_File bs=1M count=512
10. Check MD5: md5sum /root/512M_File
11. Copy the file to RAID: cp /root/512M_File /mnt/raid
12. Check MD5: md5sum /root/512M_File
 
IV. Disable Disk for only RAID 1 & 5:
13. Disable 1 of disks: mdadm --manage /dev/md3 --fail /dev/nvme2n1
14. Check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　 Check that the disable disk should show “faulty”.

15. Remove the faulty disk: mdadm --manage /dev/md3 --remove /dev/nvme2n1
16. Check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　 Check that the faulty disk should be removed.

17. Add 1 disk: mdadm --manage /dev/md3 --add /dev/nvme2n1
18. Check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　 Check that the added disk should show “spare rebuilding” in the beginning.

19. Wait for RAID rebuilding, and then check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　 Check that the added disk should become “active sync” in the end.

V. Check File:
20. Check MD5: md5sum /root/512M_File

VI. Delete RAID:
21. Umount RAID: umount /dev/md3
22. Stop RAID: mdadm --stop /dev/md3
23. Clear disks: mdadm --zero-superblock /dev/nvme2n1 /dev/nvme3n1 /dev/nvme4n1 /dev/nvme5n1
24. Check RAID: mdadm --detail /dev/md3
　 →Check RAID should disappear.

25. Check disks: lsblk

Criteria:
1. Software RAID should be created, disabled, removed, added, and rebuilt successfully.
2. File should be copied to RAID and checked with correct MD5 successfully.
3. RAID volume and disks' status should be correct in each steps.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

Inband Method 
• Total GPU Count
$ sudo lspci -d 1002:75a0 | wc -l
• PCI link status (MI350X/355X downlink port to Astera Retimer)
$ sudo lspci -d 1022:1500 -vvv | grep LnkSta:
• XGMI link status
$ amdxio -xgmi -linkstatus
• amdgpu driver loaded and all devices are visible
$ amd-smi list
Out-of-Band (OOB) Method
1. Refer to the section Collect UBB FW Info and Update UBB FW to obtain the UBB FW information.
2. Refer to the section Health Check on UBB and OAM to obtain and check the UBB and OAMs health status.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check GPU unidirectional bandwidth
1. Install TransferBench using the following command:
#git clone -b develop https://github.com/ROCmSoftwarePlatform/TransferBench
2. The TransferBench app takes a config filename that specifies which data transfers to make and an optional size parameter. The size parameter defaults to bytes, but supports KB, MB, and GB as well. The CFG mode syntax is as follows:
[NUM_WARMUPS=<#iterations>][NUM_ITERATIONS=<#iterations>] ./ TransferBench
<Config File> [<size>[K|M|G]]
This test primarily relies on TransferBench's P2P overall matrix mode instead of using the config file mode. P2P mode generates all permutations of point-to-point unidirectional and bidirectional transfers and collects the overall results in two output tables, for unidirectional and bidirectional transfers respectively. The syntax for P2P mode is:
NUM_WARMUPS=<#iterations>][NUM_ITERATIONS=<#iterations>]
USE_GPU_DMA=1 ./TransferBench p2p [<size>[K|M|G]].
3. Send large (1GB) unidirectional data transfers between all CPU and GPU device combinations.
4. Execute the unidirectional and bidirectional P2P test using the following command:
>> USE_GPU_DMA=1 ./TransferBench p2p 1G
5. Verify that all unidirectional transfers (the first output table) exceed the minimum GB/s specification. When using the P2P mode, TransferBench will use Local Read/Remote Write for data transfers. To test Remote Read/Local Write data transfers on the CPU, use the following command which uses TransferBench's CFG mode with the cpu.cfgfile listed below:
./TransferBench cpu.cfg 1G
cpu.cfg:
1  104  (C0 D0 G0)
1  104  (C0 D1 G1)
...
1  104  (C0 D7 G7)
#remote GPU- remote Read
1  104  (C1 D0 G0)
1  104  (C1 D1 G1)
...
1  104  (C1 D7 G7)

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

After setup, run the mi300_bandwidth harness and compare the resulting metric vs the AMD GPU spec/reference.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Prerequisite: Prior to testing, set the NUMA Balancing command to "Disable". 
#echo 0 | sudo tee/proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing
2. Begin GPU logging. Monitor and collect from all GPUs: Power Consumption, Thermal Hotspot Temperature, GFXCLK Frequency at 1000 ms period.
>> sudo ./agt -i=0,5,10,15,20,25,30,35 -unilog=PM -unilogallgroups -unilogperiod=1000 -unilogoutput=pm_xxx.csv
3. Start system logging. Poll, monitor and collect: Ambient Inlet Temperature, System Fan Speeds, Power Supply Output Power. Collect these data via BMC.
$ipmitool sensor list
Note : Continue logging and record sensor
4. Idle for 3 minutes
5. Run the workload RVS GST module for 30 minutes. Be sure to capture output logs showing GFLOP performance per DGEMM run within the looped test. Kill the RVS process after running it for 30 minutes.
>> /opt/rocm/bin/rvs -c /opt/rocm/share/rocm-validation-suite/conf/gst_stress_12_hrs.conf
6.Allow the system (GPUs and CPUs) to Idle for a minimum of one (1) minute to allow the following:
– temperatures to decrease
– GPU GFXCLKs to dynamically transition to lower power states
– System Fan speeds to decrease
– Power Supply loads to decrease.
This idle wait period will effectively create a distinct log data signature to allow data synchronization more easily between the individual GPU logs, system logs, and DGEMM output logs, especially when they may have different sampling periods.
7. Finalize the test. Stop all logging and collect all log files. Pull and scrub the system logs for any GPU- reported errors. Graph the relevant data with a common X-axis so that events correlate across plots. The idle periods before and after the test will help align samples, especially where the system, GPU or workload logs have different sampling periods. Allow the full vertical range on the Y-axis for Power and fan speed. Focus the Y-axis range on the Y-axis for: GPU TGP, GPU Temp, GPU GFXCLK, DGEMM GFLOPs.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.To execute AMDXIO to grab PCIe margin data on all links. Checking the BDF mapping is required.
BDF may change depending on sBIOS version. Run PCIe link status command below to get correct BDF (Target the PCIebridge)

>> sudo ./amdxio -i=0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28 -pcie -list -ports
2. Determine which BDF (Bus/Device/Function) to target with the tool: 
>> lspci | grep 1500
From the resulting output, record all BDF number information. 
3. Disable ASPM on any link to be margined.
Using the BDF information from step 2, from a command line terminal, issue the following command to disable ASPM for every link to be used in margining:
$sudo ./amdxio -pcieaspmcontrol -seg=0 -bn=<b#> -dn=<d#> -fn=<f#> -disable_L1 -disable_L0s
Using the BDF info in step 2, insert appropriate number into desired field of the command. Example:
– b# - Bus#: 0a
– d# - Dev#: 00
– f# - Func#: 0
For BDF 0a:00.0, this command would be:
$sudo ./amdxio -pcieaspmcontrol -seg=0 -bn=0a -dn=00 -fn=0 -disable_L1 -disable_L0s
4. Run PCIe Margin commands to collect desired PCIe margin data:
Open a command line terminal for each command to run, and type in the following to start margin testing based on the BDF information gathered previously. Construct each command to target the desired BDF/link (for a total of 8 links on an AMD GPUX system).
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 1st PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 2nd PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 3rd PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 4th PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 5th PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 6th PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 7th PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
$sudo ./amdxio -margin -pcie -bdf=<insert bdf# for 8th PCIe link> -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -receiver=6 -4pt -phaseleftrange=8:0.8 -phaserightrange=6:0.6 -dactoprange=6:0.6 -dacbotrange=7:0.7
5. After the test are completed, results are collected inside an AMDXIO folder. Collect these files for analysis of margin/results data.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
Check the UI and mV on the console output or result logs. The results should be equal to or below the reference results.

The csv file that is generated contains the following columns of information. Review columns: 
Margin Left (UI) 
Margin Right (UI) 
Margin Top (volt) 
Margin Bottom (volt) 
Use the following criteria to determine the outcome of the test: 
PASS = Every lane (row) in .csv result file shows a non-zero value for the above columns. 
FAIL = A value of zero ("0") is observed in any of above columns. This indicates that the lane did not meet the screening criteria (step value).
items.ai_commands: -- PCIe 4-point margin test needs the AMDXIO margin test run + console/UI mV results; agent runs the margin test and captures the mV report for lanes under test.
items.ai_logs_output: return the 4-point margin output (mV per lane) so user checks values are within the reference limit. Long runtime - approval.

    Use the XGMI margin (RX) to provide signal integrity coverage. This ensures an optimal margin on broad system-level coverage. The four-point test method is used to validate that the XGMI lane margins meet the quality metrics in eye height (EH) center and eye width (EW).
1. Execute AMDXIO to grab XGMI margin data on all links.

items.items: Updated firmware for all baseboard components will activate after AC power cycle
items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.	Equip Vulcan, and then power-on SUT, so that HGX can be connected to MB.
2.	Check current DGX firmware in Client :
curl -ks -u admin:admin 'https://<BMC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory?$expand=.($levels=1)' | jq -r '.Members[]|(.Id + "version=\"" + .Version + "\"")'
3.	Flash DGX firmware:
a.	Set target to “HGX_0”:
echo "{\"Targets\":[\"/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/HGX_0\"]}" > parameters_<BMC_IP>.json

b.	Flash DGX firmware:
curl -k -u admin:admin -H 'Expect:' --location --request POST https://<BMC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/upload -F 'UpdateParameters=@parameters_<BMC_IP>.json;type=application/json' -F UpdateFile=@<Bundle_image>.fwpkg | python3 -m json.tool
→ Get <TaskID>

c.	Continue to check New-Task’s progress until it shows “"TaskStats": "Completed"“:
curl -s -k -u admin:admin https://<BMC_IP>/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/1 | jq -r | tail -n 6

d.	Power-Cycle SUT

4.	Check DGX firmware again:
a.	Check current DGX firmware again:
Run below cmd in R340 (Client)：
curl -ks -u admin:admin 'https://<BMC_IP>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory?$expand=.($levels=1)' | jq -r '.Members[]|(.Id + "version=\"" + .Version + "\"")'

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Flash firmware without error.
2. New firmware version should be correct.
items.ai_packages_needed: NVIDIA flash tooling (nvflash / nvsm update) + user-provided image
items.ai_commands: -- Updated firmware for all baseboard components will activate after AC power cycle requires the target component's flash image + an AC power cycle by operator to activate; agent can only do the in-band flash step and verify version after reboot. Confirm exact image + component + expected new version with user first.
items.ai_logs_output: return flash log, then after the operator performs the AC power cycle verify the new firmware version via `nvsm show firmware`/nvflash.
items.risk: RISK: firmware flash + AC cycle is state-changing and can require recovery; flash only the exact user-specified component/image and confirm the SUT is ready.

items.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.

    【During Test】
    1. Bootinto OS and login with the root.
2. Make sure all GPUs can detected under OS : lspci |grep NV
3. Make sure all GPUs listed from nvidia-smi : nvidia-smi
4. Stop nvidia-fabricmanager : systemctl stop nvidia-fabricmanager
6. Get all GPUs UUID : nvidia-smi -q
7. ./rmmod_driver​
8. modprobe nvidia NVreg_GpuBlacklist=UUID1,UUID2,....
9. cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params​
10. Start nvidia-fabricmanager : systemctl start nvidia-fabricmanager
11. nvidia-smi -B
12. run stress and check the result should without black list.

    【After Test】

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    This test performs CUDA Peer-To-Peer (P2P) data transfers between pairs of GPUs and computes latency and bandwidth. Both Copy Engine (CE) and SM types of transfers are performed. There is no pass or fail criteria for this test at this time.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. All information should be readable and no spelling error.
2. FW Version should be correct.
items.ai_packages_needed: nvqual (NVIDIA proprietary qualification tool, user installs) + NVIDIA driver
items.ai_commands: -- requires NVIDIA-proprietary `nvqual` tool + driver/SDK on DUT; each sub-test is a dedicated qualification run. NOTE: nvqual is NVIDIA-proprietary - download the version matching your GPU/driver from the NVIDIA portal before running. NOTE: nvqual is NVIDIA-proprietary - download the version matching your GPU/driver from the NVIDIA portal before running. NOTE: nvqual is NVIDIA-proprietary - download the version matching your GPU/driver from the NVIDIA portal before running. NOTE: nvqual is NVIDIA-proprietary - download the version matching your GPU/driver from the NVIDIA portal before running. Run: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvqual p2p 2>&1 | tee /tmp/nvqual.log 2>&1"
items.ai_logs_output: return full GPU peer-to-peer output; confirm info is readable, FW version is correct, and no unexpected errors. Sub-test duration varies - confirm user approval. No reboot needed for read-out runs.

$ sudo apt-get update
$ sudo apt install doca-tools

II. InstallSoftware on Host:

$ dpkg -i <repo_file>

3. Install DOCA SDK, DOCA runtime, DOCA tools:
$ sudo apt-get update
$ sudo apt install -y doca-runtime doca-sdk doca-tools
$ sudo apt install -y sshpass
$ sudo apt install -y numactl
$ sudo apt install -y ipmitool
$ sudo apt install -y python3-paramiko
$ sudo apt install -y python3-prettytable
$ sudo apt install -y python3-matplotlib

III. Check device ID of DPU:
mst start
mst status -v

module run start. Open a new terminal, add a command dmesg-follow during

Failure signature: GPU throttle in the conditions mentioned above or
during basic operation. 
No System assertion failure
No GPU initialization failure
No GPU enumeration drop failure

after the run, and in dmesg logs, key components for the GPU is initialized
successfully during a run. A failed initialization would result to a test run
failure.
Additional failure includes system unresponsive, system reboot, system
shutdown, and system power off that requires immediate attention to
verify in the BMC.
63917

condition

items.procedure:
1. Install the latest version of Intel System Stress & Memory Diagnostics.
    Decompress package
    Example, on Linux: tar xvzf ssmd_<2024.06.24.ace4>_lin.tar.gz
2. Install kernel modules / drivers
    Linux: CPU Access (details below):
2.1 Ubuntu or any of its variations
    $sudo apt-get update
    $sudo apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)
    $sudo apt install gcc-12

2.2 Build and Install CPU Access Kernel Module:
    $cd Drivers
    $make
    $sudo insmod cpuaccess.ko

2.3 User should see a device driver being loaded in /dev/cpuaccess.
    $ls /dev/cpuaccess

2.4 After succesful build and completion of above steps, if user wants to add this as part of Linux boot process:
    $make bootupdate

2.5 For further details on build options for this module, user can refer to ReadMe.md provided in ""Drivers"" folder.
3. Run workloads, to stress CPU for the max power for 1 hrs 
    $sudo ./ssmd -f flowStressTdp<Program>.json -u oc_enable=1
4. Optionally, observe system telemetry using SSMON 
CPU Profile:    
$sudo ./ssmon -p 1 -l 2
All Profile:    
$sudo ./ssmon -p 3 -l 2

5. Optionally, list system information
items.criteria:
Criteria:
1. After stress, system should be workable, and no unexpected error message generates.
2. CPU should be stressed up and without hangs during the stress.

items.procedure:
1. SSH into BMC console and execute the following command to check for current CPER index:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
2. Execute the following command for getting card ID for all devices:
$ sudo amdgpuras -l | grep /dev/dri/card
3. Execute the following command to list down current Retired Bad Page of device_id = 0:
$ cat /sys/class/drm/card<card_id>/device/ras/gpu_vram_bad_pages
4. Execute the following command for GFX poison consumption handling with ODECC injection to
device_id = 0, block_id = 2 (GFX):
$ sudo amdgpuras -d 0 -b 2 -t 8
5. SSH into BMC Console and repeat Step 1 to check for current CPER index again after injection:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries' | grep -o '""Id"": ""[^""]*' | grep -o '[0-9]*$' | sort -n | tail -1
6. SSH into BMC console and run the following command to download that generated CPER file into BMC from SMC:
# curl -X GET 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/Dump/Entries/<cper_index>/attachment' --output /tmp/<cper_index>.cper

compared later.

items.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this Margin test defines its condition by environment the agent cannot set: the chamber must hold the temperature at 40CC and a programmable AC source must hold the 5V/3.3V rails at 5V/3.3V at +5%. That condition REQUIRES a physical lab operator to place the DUT in the thermochamber and set the PSU margin. The test pumps 12h of SST network stress through every PCIe slot; without the chamber+PSU the result is not a valid margin measurement. Agent cannot create the thermal/voltage environment or the long-running stress (>=12h) must be supervised by the operator in the lab over SSH.
items.ai_logs_output: operator places DUT in thermochamber at 40CC with PSU 5V/3.3V at +5%, runs the stress, and captures SEL/BMC/dmesg event logs + test photos; agent could only post-process the collected logs/screenshots afterwards (e.g. grep SEL for errors) once the operator finishes the run.
items.risk: RISK: environmental chamber + adjustable-PSU voltage margin test; requires physical lab operator to set temperature/voltage and (for AC cycle/drop) to operate power. Do not auto-run.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Connect SUT and test client with cable direct connection.
2. Install latest NIC driver on SUT and test client.
3. Assign IP address to SUT and test client, make sure they communicate with each other.
4. Clear bmc sel.
5. Run network stress with SST for 12 hours.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Throughput result should higher than 80% of bandwidth, for example, 1G NIC should get 800M or higher result, check system loading, memory and NIC use rate, ensure system is stable.
2. Check bmc sel without  error.
items.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this Margin test defines its condition by environment the agent cannot set: the chamber must hold the temperature at 0CC and a programmable AC source must hold the 5V/3.3V rails at 5V/3.3V at -5%. That condition REQUIRES a physical lab operator to place the DUT in the thermochamber and set the PSU margin. The test pumps 12h of SST network stress through every PCIe slot; without the chamber+PSU the result is not a valid margin measurement. Agent cannot create the thermal/voltage environment or the long-running stress (>=12h) must be supervised by the operator in the lab over SSH.
items.ai_logs_output: operator places DUT in thermochamber at 0CC with PSU 5V/3.3V at -5%, runs the stress, and captures SEL/BMC/dmesg event logs + test photos; agent could only post-process the collected logs/screenshots afterwards (e.g. grep SEL for errors) once the operator finishes the run.
items.risk: RISK: environmental chamber + adjustable-PSU voltage margin test; requires physical lab operator to set temperature/voltage and (for AC cycle/drop) to operate power. Do not auto-run.

items.procedure: Follow intel Server System Validation Manual Guide
items.criteria: behavior follow the specification
items.ai_commands: -- LTSSM (PCIe Link Margin): follow the Intel Server System Validation Manual for link margin behavior. Requires the Intel validation/margin tooling and hardware setup, an operator/lab activity the agent cannot drive.
items.ai_logs_output: operator runs the Intel LTSSM margin flow per the validation manual and compares behavior to the specification; agent has no Intel tooling.

items.procedure: Run "dmidecode --type 46" under OS to read SMBIOS Type 46 (String Property).
items.criteria: Information should match SPEC definition.
items.ai_commands: -- Type 46 - String Property: run dmidecode --type 46 to read the SMBIOS Type 46 (String Property) table. A pure read sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmidecode --type 46 2>&1; echo "---exit $?---" 2>&1" ; confirm info matches SPEC.
items.ai_logs_output: return the full dmidecode --type 46 output so the operator confirms the string properties match SPEC.

items.procedure:
1. Enter BMC-Web -> Operations -> Firmware Update.
2. Click "Browser" -> browse firmware-file (.ima) -> click "Start firmware upgrade".
3. Click "Preserve all Configuration …" -> click "Proceed to Flash" -> clecik "Yes".
4. After flash completion, check firmware version.
items.criteria:
1. Flash firmware without error.
2. After flash completion, firmware version should be correct.
items.ai_packages_needed: BMC BIOS .ima image (user-designated) + BMC credentials + image upload path
items.ai_commands: -- Flash BIOS Firmware - upgrade: upgrade BIOS via BMC-web -> Operations -> Firmware Update (browse the .ima firmware file -> Start firmware upgrade -> Preserve config -> Proceed to Flash -> Yes). This is a BMC web-UI action needing the user-designated BIOS image; agent can drive the Redfish UpdateService equivalent (POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService/Actions/UpdateService.Update with the image) and then verify the new version, once the image path is confirmed.  -- duplicate Flash-BIOS-upgrade instance; verify a clean upgrade + correct BIOS version as in the sibling row.
items.ai_logs_output: return the flash action result (Redfish UpdateService POST) + the firmware version before/after via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory" 2>&1 | grep -iE "Name|Version|Id" 2>&1" so the user confirms the upgrade flashed without error and the version is correct.
items.risk: RISK: flashing BIOS is state-changing and can break the BMC/host if interrupted; only flash the user-specified image and never power-cut mid-flash.

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Operations -> OEM firmware.
2. Click "Browser" -> browse firmware-file (.ima) -> click "Start firmware upgrade".
3. Click "Preserve all Configuration …" -> click "Proceed to Flash" -> clecik "Yes".
4. After flash completion, check firmware version.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
items.criteria:
1. Flash firmware without error.
2. After flash completion, firmware version should be correct.
items.ai_packages_needed: BMC CPLD .ima image (user-designated) + BMC credentials + image upload path
items.ai_commands: -- Flash CPLD Firmware: upgrade CPLD via BMC-web -> Operations -> Firmware Update (browse the .ima firmware file -> Start firmware upgrade -> Preserve config -> Proceed to Flash -> Yes). This is a BMC web-UI action needing the user-designated CPLD image; agent can drive the Redfish UpdateService equivalent (POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService/Actions/UpdateService.Update with the image) and then verify the new version, once the image path is confirmed.
items.ai_logs_output: return the flash action result (Redfish UpdateService POST) + the firmware version before/after via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory" 2>&1 | grep -iE "Name|Version|Id" 2>&1" so the user confirms the upgrade flashed without error and the version is correct.
items.risk: RISK: flashing CPLD is state-changing and can break the BMC/host if interrupted; only flash the user-specified image and never power-cut mid-flash.
